title: Shipping Clerk
description:
Compensation Range:

$ 25.00



We are looking for an organized shipping clerk to handle all the service order shipments – including ordered and fabricated parts to pack list specifications.

When needed this person will assist the shipping coordinator in the responsibilities for arranging over dimensional and other contract-based shipments based on production schedule and customer demands. The shipping clerk is also responsible for tracking shipments.

Also, when required this employee will need to assist in arranging inbound freight from Munter’s vendors.

To be successful as a shipping clerk, one must have a solid understanding and working knowledge of parcel, LTL, TL, and international shipping practices. Excellent attention to detail. A great shipping clerk can successfully multitask several tasks at once. The shipping clerk should be able to ensure efficient and cost-effective supply chain operations. They should be able to assist in the prompt resolution of any issues and have strong negation skills. Excellent communication skills are a must.

  • Create all required shipping documents for all outbound loads (BOLs, pack list, NAFTA/USMCA, Commercial Invoices, etc.)
  • Promptly ship all service orders, following the process until completion.
  • Package all outgoing service orders properly (banding, wrapping, shrink wrapping, crating, etc.)
  • Handle all return shipments and documentation.
  • Communicate all shipment tracking and follow up with the appropriate personnel.
  • Resolve/report any issues during transit.
  • Prepare shipping quotes for service personnel and/or customers.
  • Handle all freight claims until resolved.
  • Negotiate shipping fees with couriers.
  • Prepare reports for management.
  • Keep a meticulous record of shipment information.
  • Computer literacy skills.
  • Flexible work hours.
  • Excellent time management skills.
  • Ability to multitask.
  • Ability to read a tape measure.
  • Review freight invoices for billing accuracy and approval.
  • Takes initiative and self-motivated.
  • Back up for scheduling/arranging inbound freight.
  • Other tasks as assigned by manager.

Required Education:

High school diploma or GED, college preferred.

Job Qualifications:

1-3 years in dispatch or traffic management experience.

Training Requirements:

Munters new employee orientation, quality assurance and safety awareness

Hours of Work:

Standard work schedule plus overtime and weekend hours will be required to meet production needs.

title: Horticulturalist (Indoor and Outdoor Gardens) Saudi Arabia
description:
We are looking for qualified and experienced horticulture professionals to join the KAUST Beacon Development team and support the development and maintenance of high-quality indoor and outdoor garden environments.

Positions

  • Horticulturalist – Indoor Gardens – 5+ years’ experience
  • Assistant Horticulturalist – Outdoor Gardens – 3+ years’ experience

Responsibilities

  • Plan and carry out daily horticulture activities across indoor and outdoor garden environments.
  • Plant, establish, maintain, prune, propagate, replace, and care for a wide range of plants.
  • Maintain trees, shrubs, groundcovers, herbaceous plants, seasonal displays, and indoor plant collections.
  • Monitor plant health and identify pests, diseases, nutrient deficiencies, water stress, and environmental issues.
  • Implement and support Integrated Pest Management (IPM) strategies.
  • Monitor and manage irrigation, watering, fertilisation, soil/media, and growing conditions.
  • Maintain high horticultural, aesthetic, cleanliness, and presentation standards.
  • Support seasonal planting and garden maintenance programmes.
  • Assist with plant identification, labelling, inventory, collection records, and maintenance records.
  • Monitor indoor environmental conditions including light, temperature, and humidity where applicable.
  • Maintain and safely operate horticulture tools and equipment.
  • Identify and report damaged, declining, hazardous, or poorly performing plants.
  • Support routine and preventive horticulture maintenance activities.
  • Work collaboratively with horticulturists, gardeners, botanists, landscape teams, irrigation personnel, contractors, and other garden operations teams.
  • Maintain clean, organised, and safe horticulture work areas.
  • Follow all applicable health, safety, environmental, biosecurity, and horticulture procedures.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Horticulture, Botany, Plant Sciences, or a related discipline.
  • Horticulturalist – Indoor Gardens: Minimum 5+ years of relevant professional experience.
  • Assistant Horticulturalist – Outdoor Gardens: Minimum 3+ years of relevant professional experience.
  • Strong practical knowledge of horticulture, plant care, cultivation, and maintenance.
  • Experience in indoor gardens, conservatories, glasshouses, botanic gardens, public gardens, nurseries, landscapes, or similar environments.
  • Experience with planting, pruning, propagation, watering, fertilisation, mulching, and plant replacement.
  • Knowledge of plant identification and plant-health management.
  • Experience identifying and managing common pests, diseases, nutrient deficiencies, and environmental stresses.
  • Knowledge or experience in Integrated Pest Management (IPM).
  • Experience with irrigation and water-management practices.
  • Knowledge of soil preparation, growing media, fertilisation, and plant nutrition.
  • For the Indoor Gardens position, experience managing controlled indoor growing environments including light, temperature, and humidity is required.
  • Experience maintaining plant records, inventories, and maintenance documentation.
  • Ability to safely use and maintain horticulture tools and equipment.
  • Strong teamwork, communication, planning, and problem-solving skills.
  • Previous experience in a botanic garden, conservatory, glasshouse, public garden, arboretum, nursery, or major landscape environment is preferred.
  • Additional training or professional certification in horticulture, plant health, IPM, irrigation, or related areas is an advantage.
  • Master’s degree in a relevant discipline is preferred for the Horticulturalist – Indoor Gardens position.

title: Werkstudent Data, Privacy & Cybersecurity
description:
Keen to become part of a truly global, collaborative team of professionals? Your journey begins here.

Waar ga je werken?

Hogan Lovells behoort tot de grootste internationale advocatenkantoren en heeft meer dan 35 kantoren in Afrika, Azië, Europa, Latijns Amerika, het Midden Oosten en de Verenigde Staten. Wereldwijd werken meer dan 2800 juristen bij Hogan Lovells waarvan circa 70 advocaten, (kandidaat-) notarissen, fiscalisten en paralegals in Amsterdam. Bij Hogan Lovells krijg je de kans om zowel jouw eigen toekomst als die van onze cliënten vorm te geven.


Wat kun je verwachten?

Als werkstudent draai je gedurende drie maanden circa twee dagen per week volwaardig mee in het hechte Data, Privacy & Cybersecurity-team in Amsterdam, waar open en duidelijke communicatie centraal staat. Je zal een kamer delen met een ervaren advocaat die je persoonlijk begeleidt en daarnaast wordt een begeleider toegewezen. Je mag iedere week deelnemen aan ons koffieoverleg zodat je precies weet wat er op de afdeling speelt en waar iedereen zich mee bezighoudt.


Wij adviseren cliënten over uiteenlopende, strategische vraagstukken op het gebied van Data, Privacy & Cybersecurity. Hierbij kan onder andere gedacht worden aan advisering met betrekking tot wereldwijde cyberaanvallen en datalekken, AVG compliance, (internationale) doorgifte en uitwisseling van persoonsgegevens, cookies, het gebruik van data uit medische hulpmiddelen en handhaving door de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens. Onze cliënten zijn onder andere grote (beursgenoteerde) bedrijven, tech bedrijven in de reissector, wereldwijde cloudaanbieders, sportmerken, fabrikanten van zelfrijdende auto's, fabrikanten van connected medische hulpmiddelen en softwareleveranciers.


Innovation & Inclusion en Responsible Business zijn belangrijke prioriteiten voor ons kantoor. Hogan Lovells behoort tot de top 5 van meest innovatieve advocatenkantoren in Noord-Amerika en Europa. Het doen van pro bono- en vrijwilligerswerk zit in het DNA van onze mensen. Op deze manier nemen we onze verantwoordelijkheid om iets terug te geven aan de maatschappij.


Wat ga je doen?

Je taken zijn breed en divers, variërend van het analyseren van nieuwe wetgeving en juridische vraagstukken, het schrijven van interne memo's, blogs en conceptadviezen, tot het bijwonen van besprekingen met cliënten. Onder begeleiding van onze advocaten zal je daarbij worden geleerd hoe je de theorie naar de praktijk vertaalt, om zo tot voor de cliënt praktisch werkbare adviezen te komen die recht doen aan de belangen van de cliënt. Daarnaast is er ruimte voor eigen initiatieven en verantwoordelijkheden. Uiteraard ben je ook welkom bij al onze sociale activiteiten en ontmoet je ook advocaten, werkstudenten en student-stagiairs van andere praktijkgroepen. Zo krijg je een goed beeld van Hogan Lovells, ons team en hoe het is om daarvan onderdeel uit te maken.


Wie ben jij?

  • Je bent een initiatiefrijke en ambitieuze student in de eindfase van je master (civiel effect), met goede studieresultaten (WO);
  • Je hebt aantoonbare affiniteit en/of werkervaring in Data, Privacy & Cybersecurity;
  • Je hebt oog voor detail en kan (zeer) nauwkeurig werken; en
  • Je beheerst de Nederlandse en Engelse taal uitstekend in woord en geschrift.

Geïnteresseerd?

Indien je wilt solliciteren klik je op de ‘apply’ button. Nadat je een account hebt aangemaakt kan je je gegevens invullen en je stukken uploaden. We ontvangen graag je CV, motivatiebrief, cijferlijsten en eventuele (stage)beoordelingen.


Vergeet niet in je motivatiebrief te vermelden per wanneer je beschikbaar bent. Op dit moment hebben wij plek vanaf december 2026.


Voor vragen kan je contact opnemen met Ariëlle Hulst (Campus Recruiter) via telefoonnummer 020-5533660 of per mail: amsterdam.recruitment@hoganlovells.com.

title: SQA MRA to Spec Lead (2-year assignment)
description:
Job Description:

The SQA MRA to Spec Lead (2-year assignment) is is a pivotal strategic role responsible for defining, aligning, and accelerating global processes. This role drives the digital transformation of material and supplier qualification globally across all Pet Nutrition business units .

By mapping existing workflows, identifying bottlenecks, and translating complex process data into technical requirements, the Lead will establish an accelerated "To-Be" qualification framework that reduces time-to-market without compromising on compliance, quality, or safety. Acting as the ultimate bridge between technical IT/Data teams and business operations, this position orchestrates process automation and champions data hygiene,

The role is also responsible for defining globally harmonized supplier quality performance management process including KPIs, Metrics and dashboard design supporting the process.

Accountable for successful deployment and adoption of the processes, automation and tracking by the business.


Context and Scope:

Operating in a highly dynamic and regulated environment, this role must balance agility with strict adherence to quality and safety standards. The role requires significant stakeholder management, working seamlessly at global level across different business units, segments, global R&D networks, IT partners, and third-party supplier bases. Successful execution will directly impact the speed of innovation and supply chain resilience by bringing safe, high-quality products to market faster.


What would be your key responsibilities?


Global Process Standardization & Qualification Acceleration

  • Best Practice Mapping: Conduct global, cross-segment mapping exercises to capture, document, and benchmark "As-Is" material and supplier qualification workflows.
  • Bottleneck Identification: Pinpoint operational bottlenecks, redundancies, and regional variances that delay the supplier onboarding cycle. Translate complex process mining outputs into tangible, actionable technical and business requirement documents.
  • Time-to-Market Optimization: Standardize global "To-Be" qualification procedures to establish a robust, compliant "fast-track" or accelerated qualification framework.
  • R&D & Supplier Co-Creation: Co-create a connected process with R&D, external suppliers, and cross-functional partners to support efficient, real-time collaboration.
  • Continuous Improvement: Act as the strategic bridge between technical data analysts and business operations to prioritize and implement process-refining features.
  • Global Quality Templates: Ensure aligned global templates integrate distinct material category qualification requirements and respect pet-food-specific regulatory standards, safety margins, and raw material nuances.

Supplier Performance & Relationship Management Framework

  • Joint Process Definition: Lead the co-design of the global supplier quality performance management process with internal partners and key strategic suppliers to foster mutual accountability.

Data Analytics, KPIs, and Dashboard Governance

  • KPI Validation: Partner with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), Quality Engineers, and Data Engineering teams to validate, refine, and sign off on standardized KPIs for supplier quality performance.
  • Dashboard Co-Creation: Lead the development of intuitive supplier performance dashboards, ensuring underlying data pipelines from enterprise systems are accurate, robust, and globally standardized.
  • Data Hygiene Advocacy: Support business units to ensure data quality at the source for reliable, xxxx accurate reporting by actively connecting business operations with data experts and resources.

Process Automation & Digital Tool Orchestration

  • Automation Pipeline Scopes: Collaborate with Digital, IT, and Systems teams to identify high-potential targets for workflow automation.
  • System Integrations: Help define the technical and business scope for connecting core platforms (such as Quality Management Systems, ERPs/S4 HANA, and supplier collaboration hubs).
  • Technology Pilot Leadership: Scope, test, and pilot innovative digital quality tools before launching them to the wider global business network.

What are we looking for?

  • Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Quality Management, Food Safety, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related technical discipline is beneficial.
  • Consistent experience in technical function, ideally across SQA/R&D/Q&FS.
  • Experience implementing projects with senior x-functional stakeholders.
  • Preferred: Certifications in Lean Six Sigma (Green/Black Belt), Business Process Management (BPM), Agile Project Management, or Change Management.
  • Consistent experience in Quality Systems, SQA, Manufacturing Quality, or Supply Chain Operations within the FMCG, food, or pharmaceutical industries.
  • Process Mapping Mastery: Proven experience leading end-to-end business process mapping and design (e.g., Value Stream Mapping) to drive efficiency and lean operations.
  • Digital Strategy & Collaboration: Experience collaborating directly with Digital/IT functions to co-create long-term roadmaps, deploy enterprise-level digital tools, or drive large-scale digital transformations.
  • Systems & Database Expertise: Deep understanding of enterprise quality and specification management software (experience with Mars-specific systems such as Nexus, Trinity, and ATLAS, or equivalents like SAP QM and PLM systems is highly advantageous).

What can you expect from Mars?

  • Work with diverse and talented Associates, all guided by the Five Principles.
  • Join a purpose-driven company, where we’re striving to build the world we want tomorrow, today.
  • Best-in-class learning and development support from day one, including access to our in-house Mars University.
  • An industry-competitive salary and benefits package, including a company bonus.

Mars is committed to providing access, equal opportunity, and reasonable adjustments for individuals with disabilities, long-term health conditions, or who are neurodiverse during the application and recruitment process. To request reasonable adjustments, complete our Reasonable Adjustment Request Form here

title: Loss Prevention Representative (LPR)
description:
Excited to grow your career?

At Chevron Stations Inc (CSI), we sell gasoline and convenience products at our retail stations. We are looking for hard working people who value safety, enjoy working as a team and have a positive work attitude. The perfect fit for our team are individuals who are self-motivated, dependable and able to work effectively & safely in a fast-paced environment while maintaining 100% total customer focus.

People First, Excellence Always

Job Expectations

  • Maintain courteous, professional contact with co-workers, customers, vendors, and community at large.

  • Maintain neat appearance and good personal hygiene in compliance with CSI image and uniform standards.

  • Support and follow established safety, security, quality guidelines as well as CSI’s policies, procedures, practices, and programs. Report accidents or incidents to the manager immediately.

  • Preserve safety of self, fellow employees, and all others in the work location by utilizing the CSI Loss Prevention process.

  • Regular and punctual attendance is required.

Essential Functions:

  • Provide exceptional guest service. Greet and thank all customers, respond to customer questions, and assist customers to find products.

  • Ensures the safety and security of our guests, team members, and property.

  • using company processes, involving the appropriate people in emergency situations, and communicating all significant incidents

  • Aware of actionable insights to mitigate shortage risks in order to drive sales, improve accuracy and in-stocks through theft prevention and resolution, and lead through emergency events to protect our guest, team and brand.

  • Provide a strong and friendly visual presence to deter theft and other criminal activities and to ensure a safe and comfortable environment for employees and customers.

  • Regularly patrol and monitor the station, including internal and exterior property parking lots and fuel islands.

  • Be attentive, observant, and alert, promptly report any unusual occurrences, as appropriate, to facility management or law enforcement; prepare written report as requested.

  • Respond appropriately to security and safety issues, leverage de-escalation techniques and other tools in accordance with CSI’s policies.

  • Provides required documentation of stations incidents and activities to the station management.

  • Other duties as assigned by management include:

    • Station cleaning of the indoor and outdoor facilities including restrooms, islands, pumps, and car wash, if applicable.

    • Display goods in an orderly manner throughout the store and continuously ensure shelves are full of products. This includes both the retail space and cooler locations in the store.

Requirement/Qualifications:

  • Must be sufficiently proficient in English to understand CSI policies, safety training, and job instructions, and to effectively communicate with customers and/or coworkers on work-related matters.

  • Available to work a variety of hours, which may include early mornings, evenings, weekends, overnight shifts, and holidays.

  • Ability to engage with customers and build positive, helpful rapport through effective and friendly communications.

  • Ability to handle challenging situations and make decisions in a timely manner. Demonstrated skills in de-escalation of customer situations.

  • Ability to write reports. Ability to understand and carry out oral and written directive.

  • Strong attention to detail.

  • Ability to work both independently and in team settings.

  • Security and loss prevention experience preferred.

Supervisor Responsibilities

title: Staff Systems Engineer (Time and Frequency)
description:
Infleqtion is a global quantum technology company solving the world’s most challenging problems. The company harnesses quantum mechanics to build and integrate quantum computers, sensors, and networks. From fundamental physics to leading edge commercial products, Infleqtion enables “quantum everywhere” through our ecosystem of devices and platforms.

As a deep-tech startup, Infleqtion embraces a results-driven, fast-paced, and customer-focused approach to innovation. We seek an experienced Staff Systems Engineer to support multidisciplinary government and commercial R&D projects.

The duties and responsibilities below describe the expected scope of ownership. Depending on business needs, this role may perform a combination of some or all of the following duties; additional duties may arise.

  • Own and manage system requirements for Time & Frequency products and programs, including customer requirement review, internal decomposition, traceability, and alignment across engineering teams.
  • Maintain Jama or equivalent requirements-management tools as the source of truth for customer requirements, derived requirements, verification methods, requirement status, version control, and change history.
  • Own and manage interface control documentation (ICDs), including source-of-truth documentation, revision control, and coordination across the physics package, lasers and optics, electronics, FPGA/firmware, software, mechanical, thermal, command-and-telemetry, and customer teams.
  • Lead verification and validation planning by mapping requirements to verification methods, defining evidence needs, coordinating test-plan inputs, and ensuring customer-facing V&V documentation is complete, consistent, and review-ready.
  • Coordinate with AI&T leads and technical teams to define, document, and oversee integration and test activities from subsystem through full-system level, including capture of performance data and preparation of results for internal and customer review.
  • Own the quality and readiness of customer-facing systems-engineering documentation, including templates, folder structure, revision control, release status, and delivery readiness.
  • Author major systems-engineering documents and assign technical sections to subject-matter experts as needed, including requirements documents, ICDs, system architecture documents, CONOPs, verification plans, test plans, design-review packages, and customer deliverables.
  • Drive Product Lifecycle execution for selected R&D, product-development, and customer programs by defining required deliverables, establishing review entry and exit criteria, preparing design-review packages, and tracking closure actions.
  • Work with the Chief Engineer and program leadership to establish a repeatable design-review structure, including standard review materials, required artifacts, action-item tracking, and customer-facing closure evidence.
  • Maintain the program risk register and support risk communication with program management and customers, including mitigation plans, assigned owners, schedule impacts, and linkage to technical decisions.
  • Support and maintain FMEA or similar failure-analysis documentation, ensuring identified failure modes are connected to requirements, design mitigations, test coverage, and program risks.
  • Own and maintain system CONOPs by working with physicists, subsystem leads, applications engineering, and customers to ensure operational concepts are consistent with system architecture, interfaces, operating modes, constraints, and intended use cases.
  • Own and maintain system architecture documentation for precision timing products, including functional allocations, subsystem responsibilities, timing and frequency-reference architecture, interfaces, operating modes, and change propagation across teams.
  • Own source-of-truth SWaP tracking by collecting updated size, weight, power, thermal, and environmental estimates from IPT leads; documenting assumptions and margins; and communicating impacts to architecture, requirements, risk, and customer deliverables.
  • Establish lean, right-sized systems-engineering processes suitable for deep-tech R&D, product development, and customer deployment without creating unnecessary process burden.
  • Ensure consistent use of systems-engineering tools and methods across selected programs, including requirements management, configuration control, document control, review readiness, traceability, and change management.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, physics, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of progressive systems engineering experience with complex hardware/software systems, ideally including quantum systems, precision sensors, aerospace systems, spacecraft payloads, or other multidisciplinary R&D systems.
  • Demonstrated ability to own requirements from customer-level intent through internal decomposition, traceability, change control, and verification planning.
  • Experience developing or maintaining ICDs across electrical, mechanical, optical, software, command/telemetry, and customer interfaces.
  • Experience creating V&V plans, test plans, verification matrices, and customer-ready evidence packages for complex technical systems.
  • Experience with configuration management, document control, revision control, and formal technical review processes.
  • Ability to learn enough technical depth in complex physics, hardware, electronics, software, and integration/test systems to drive practical systems engineering decisions and keep teams aligned.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with engineers, physicists, program managers, customers, and subcontractors in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
  • Professional-level written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to turn incomplete technical inputs into clear customer-facing documentation.

Preferred skills:

  • Hands-on experience with Jama, DOORS, Polarion, or comparable requirements management and traceability tools.
  • Experience supporting government-funded R&D, NASA programs, aerospace payload development, or customer-facing technical reviews such as SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, or equivalent gate reviews.
  • Experience managing FMEA, risk registers, action-item logs, design-review artifacts, or technical decision records.
  • Experience with AI&T, hardware bring-up, subsystem integration, environmental testing, qualification planning, or test readiness reviews.
  • Experience owning architecture diagrams, CONOPs, SWaP budgets, or interface documentation for systems involving sensors, lasers, electronics, software, controls, or telemetry.
  • Experience helping organizations implement lean Product Life Cycle or productization processes for R&D-to-product transition.

Benefits

  • Salary Range: per year
  • 100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, short/long-term disability
  • Employer-funded Health Savings Account
  • Unlimited PTO
  • 401(k) match
  • Company-paid Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Flexible Savings Account
  • Paid FMLA, Maternity/Paternity Leave
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Student Loan Repayment
  • Equity Program

title: IT Assistant (Product Adoption and Support) SC5
description:
DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS

7 October 2026-23:59-GMT Greenwich Mean Time (Dakar)

WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.


ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.


At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.

  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.

  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

JOB TITLE: IT Assistant (Product Adoption and Support)


TYPE OF CONTRACT: Service Contract


GRADE: Level 5


UNIT/DIVISION: TECD Digital Services


DUTY STATION (City, Country): Dakar, Senegal


DURATION: 12 months



ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian agency, fighting hunger worldwide. The WFP Technology Division (TEC) is the digital business engine of the World Food Programme, providing the business with multi-pronged and resilient technical capabilities able to respond with the agility required in humanitarian operations, be they manmade or in a natural disaster setting.

TEC’s Digital Solutions Branch (TECD) oversees all solution development activities for WFP, covering the full technology stack and delivering changes to existing solutions. This function manages all aspects of development, from understanding business requirements to designing and building solutions, and overseeing quality assurance. TECD is expanding their service offering into the support and adoption of corporate tools used on the front line of WFP’s operations.

TECD’s Global Beneficiary Services (GBS) team supports the adoption and effective use of corporate IT solutions that enable programme delivery across WFP operations. GBS provides guidance, training, and Tier 2 support to Country Offices (CO) adopting these tools. Members of the team are spread across WFP’s five Regional Offices (RO) to provide follow-the-sun support in the time zone and language of our COs.


BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

Under the direct supervision of the Head of GBS, the IT Assistant - Product Adoption and Support will assist with the preparation, roll￼out, and ongoing support of corporate IT solutions. The incumbent will contribute to user readiness activities, provide timely support for incidents, and help ensure effective communication and collaboration between Country Offices and Global HQ teams.

This position requires good organization skills, the ability to handle multiple tasks, and a commitment to delivering quality support.


DUTIES:

The main responsibilities include, but are not limited to:


• Support:

o Deliver service requests and provide basic troubleshooting for incidents, escalating more complex issues to senior team members as needed.

o Help train local support teams according to standard operating procedures (SOP).


• Adoption:

o Support country offices in understanding available corporate IT solutions for programmatic activities (e.g. SCOPE, SugarCRM, NEST, CIAM, School Connect, Partner Connect, CODA, PIT).

o Assist in preparing country offices for the adoption of new tools by helping gather requirements and sharing guidance materials.


• Roll-out:

o Provide logistical and technical support during pilot deployments, helping identify issues and collect feedback.

o Contribute to training and awareness sessions to help users become familiar with new IT solutions.

o Travel on local and international missions (as required).


• Collaboration and knowledge management:

o Maintain clear and professional communication with all stakeholders.

o Share updates, lessons learned, and user feedback with the wider team to support continuous improvement.


DELIVERABLES AT THE END OF THE CONTRACT:

1. Timely and effective handling of support requests, aiming to respond to at least 90% within first point of contact (FPOC) timelines.

2. Contribution to maintaining strong incident‑resolution performance, supporting the team in meeting at least 90% SLA adherence.

3. Demonstrated growth in technical knowledge and understanding of corporate tools.

4. Active participation in documenting processes, solutions, and lessons learned to improve team knowledge management.


QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:


Education:

Completion of secondary school education. A university degree in information technology, computer science, or a related field is desirable.


Experience:

Minimum 5 years of experience in IT support, software adoption, digital tools implementation or related to the field.

Experience working in a large organisation is desirable.


Knowledge & Skills:

• Strong customer service and communication skills (clear, patient, and user‑friendly).

• Basic troubleshooting skills for common software and device issues.

• Familiarity with digital collaboration tools (e.g. Microsoft Teams, SharePoint) and IT service management systems.

•Ability to deliver simple user guidance or basic training to individuals or small groups.

• Good problem‑solving skills, attention to detail, and reliability in follow‑through.

•Enthusiasm about learning new technologies and adapting to new processes.


Languages:

Fluency (level C) in French and at least an intermediate knowledge in English (level B). Intermediate knowledge (level B) of another official UN language (Arabic or Spanish) or Portuguese (one of WFP’s working languages) is desirable.

WFP LEADERSHIP FRAMEWORK

WFP Leadership Framework guides to the common standards of behavior that guide HOW we work together to accomplish our mission.

Click here to access WFP Leadership Framework

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION

WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact: global.inclusion@wfp.org

NO FEE DISCLAIMER

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

REMINDERS BEFORE YOU SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION

  • All applications must be submitted exclusively through our online recruiting system. We do not consider CVs or applications sent by email, LinkedIn, or any other channel.

  • We strongly recommend that your Workday profile is accurate and complete, and that all sections are filled in, including your employment history, academic qualifications, language skills, and UN grade (if applicable). Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application.

  • If you experience technical issues while submitting your application, you may contact us at global.hrerecruitment@wfp.org. Please note that this email is only for technical issues with an application - unsolicited applications or documents sent to this inbox will not receive a reply.

  • At the application stage, the only required documents are your CV and Cover Letter. Additional documents (passport, certificates, recommendation letters, etc.) may be requested later in the process.

  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

All employment decisions are made on the basis of organizational needs, job requirements, merit, and individual qualifications. WFP is committed to providing an inclusive work environment free of sexual exploitation and abuse, all forms of discrimination, any kind of harassment, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. Therefore, all selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks.


No appointment under any kind of contract will be offered to members of the UN Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions (ACABQ), International Civil Service Commission (ICSC), FAO Finance Committee, WFP External Auditor, WFP Audit Committee, Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) and other similar bodies within the United Nations system with oversight responsibilities over WFP, both during their service and within three years of ceasing that service.

title: Talent Search Academic Advisor (TRIO)
description:
The University of Maine at Presque Isle is seeking a TRIO - Talent Search Academic Advisor.

The Advisor provides academic advising, career and college exploration, study skills development, financial literacy education, and individualized support to help students prepare for college success. The role involves tracking student progress, collaborating with school staff and TRIO colleagues, and connecting students to campus and community resources.

The Talent Search Academic Advisor is a key member of the TRIO Talent Search team, supporting middle and high school students in partner schools across Presque Isle, Central Aroostook, Fort Fairfield, Caswell, Limestone, Washburn, and Ashland.

This 11-month (August 15-July 15), 40-hour-per-week position is home- and school-based, with most workdays spent at partner school sites and a schedule that follows school calendars. Occasional morning, evening, weekend, and holiday hours may be required.

Candidates must have reliable means of transportation and the ability to travel as regular travel to partner schools in stated service areas are required.

This is a grant-funded, soft-money appointment, supported through a federally funded, five-year renewable TRIO Talent Search grant from the U.S. Department of Education.

For a complete list of responsibilities and qualifications, please review the full job description here.

The salary for this 11 month position is $44,000 . The university will take into consideration the salary of current UMS employees for transfer/promotion depending on skills and experience. Additional benefits include medical, retirement, dental, vision, and tuition waiver programs for employees and dependents. The UMS is a recipient of the Wellness Councils of America’s Well Workplace Award and offers wellness programs. Visit our benefits website to learn more.

Required Qualifications:

  • Baccalaureate degree in educational counseling, education, psychology, social work, or other appropriate and related field.
  • Understanding of the unique needs and challenges of working with low-income and educationally disadvantaged youth and/or adults in an educational environment.
  • Must have the ability to travel to assigned schools, including a valid driver’s license, ownership of a reliable, fully insured vehicle, and a clean driving record to drive University vehicles.
  • Deep understanding of adolescent development, paired with a proven track record of respecting, recruiting, and supporting youth from diverse social, economic, cultural, and academic backgrounds.
  • Working knowledge of secondary and postsecondary systems, student learning strategies, academic/vocational assessment tools, and group facilitation.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, strong organizational abilities, and proficiency with standard workplace technologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage priorities, exercise sound judgment, and drive outcomes independently without direct supervision.

Technology Requirements for Remote Work

  • Proof of a stable, reliable internet connection with speeds of at least 25 Mbps. Mobile hotspots are not acceptable.
  • A dedicated, distraction-free workspace that provides privacy for phone and Zoom conversations, maintains confidentiality in accordance with University policy and FERPA regulations, and accommodates a full workstation, including two monitors, docking stations, and other required equipment.
  • Ability to complete an annual Remote Work Agreement Form.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree strongly preferred in relevant fields, or individuals currently pursuing a master’s degree with required direct service experience.
  • Three or more years of related work experience.
  • Preference given to individuals who have overcome circumstances like those of the population the project serves.
  • Experience with and understanding of college admissions and financial aid processes for low-income students—particularly those who have worked in programs with objectives such as TRIO.
  • Knowledge of target schools.

How to apply

Materials must be submitted via “Apply Now" below or visit the UMPI Careers Page at http:// umpi.careers.maine.edu /.

For application to be considered complete you must create an applicant profile (application) and submit ALL of the following:

  • Cover letter
  • Resume

Important Information About the Recruitment Process:

  • For full consideration, applications must be received by October 9, 2026 at 5:00pm EST. Applications received after this date may be reviewed at the discretion of the University.
  • Finalist candidates will be asked to provide a list of professional references.
  • A background check will be conducted for the selected candidate.
  • Please note: The University is unable to consider applicants who require visa sponsorship.

About the University

For more than a century, the University of Maine at Presque Isle (UMPI) has helped students build successful professional careers. UMPI offers life-changing opportunities in a caring, small-university environment for 3,000 traditional and non-traditional students from Maine, across the United States, and around the world.

To learn more, visit the University of Maine at Presque Isle website.

Situated on 150 acres amidst the rolling hills and potato fields of northern Maine, UMPI strives to be the region’s premier learning institution while helping to stimulate cultural and economic development throughout Aroostook County and the State of Maine. Serving as an educational and cultural center for the area, university facilities host lectures, academic programs, concerts, dance performances, art exhibits, and plays that benefit the entire region. You can also explore community resources and regional attractions by reading more about what Aroostook County has to offer.

Consistent with State and Federal law, the System does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, transgender status, gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, national origin, citizenship status, familial status, ancestry, age, disability (physical or mental), genetic information, pregnancy, or veteran or military status in any aspect of its education, programs and activities, and employment. The System provides reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities upon request. If you believe you have experienced discrimination or harassment, you are encouraged to contact the System Office of Equal Opportunity and Title IX Services at 5713 Chadbourne Hall, Room 412, Orono, ME 04469-5713, by calling 207.581.1226, or via TTY at 711 (Maine Relay System). For more information about Title IX or to file a complaint, please contact the UMS Title IX Coordinator at .

title: Healthcare Airfreight Director – US
description:
About Us

Ready to rock the future with us? At Hellmann we put our people at the heart of everything we do, because for us, relationship matters. Joining us does not just mean becoming part of a global company. It is an invitation to shape the future of the logistics industry together with us. Our Hellmann culture is based on our four values: Caring, Entrepreneurial, Forward-Thinking and Reliable. These values resonate with yours? Then become part of our FAMILY that consists of around 10.000 employees in more than 200 locations worldwide.
For the better. Together.

.This position has a base compensation range of USD 150,000.00 to USD 175,000.00. In addition to this base compensation, you'll benefit from our competitive health and welfare programs, a 401(k) retirement savings plan, opportunities for tuition assistance, and incentive compensation for eligible positions. Salary determination considers your skills, experience, job location, internal pay equity and job architecture. Hellmann Worldwide Logistics regularly reviews our pay ranges against industry standards to ensure fairness.

The Healthcare Airfreight Director - US is responsible for executing Hellmann’s Healthcare Airfreight product strategy across the United States and driving the development and growth of the US Healthcare Airfreight portfolio. This role focuses on enhancing Healthcare Airfreight solutions, processes, and subject matter expertise, while supporting the Sales and Product teams throughout the US.


ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • In alignment with the Global Healthcare Airfreight Director, contribute and execute the global healthcare airfreight strategy to ensure profitable growth.
  • Establish, maintain and strengthen the relationship with vendors, i.e., airlines, packaging companies, transport companies etc., and monitor performance in cooperation with the regional and/or global healthcare quality team.
  • Provide support to internal stakeholders through meeting existing and potential customers. The focus is on supporting the teams in reference to airfreight healthcare solutions and quality aspects, collating appropriate information, assessing feasibility and providing value added solutions.
  • Work with the global and/or regional Quality team to ensure that GDP compliant policies and procedures are implemented and adhered to.
  • Direct and manage processes, i.e. Standard Operating Procedures, meeting global standards, Route Risk Assessments, CAPA etc.
  • Drive customer RFI/RFQ processes and responses either as a lead and/or in collaboration with the global airfreight healthcare team, global, regional or national sales organizations and/or the tender management team.
  • Support and/or own the implementation process of new and/or existing airfreight customers.
  • Provide best-in-class consultancy and value-added solutions to customers and internal stakeholders in reference to airfreight related products, services, e.g. packaging solutions, carrier solutions, and market developments.
  • Share best practices and, in alignment with the VIS Healthcare and global airfreight product, support training on Good Distribution Practices (GDP), packaging and airfreight solutions, if and when required to ensure that the network is up to date in critical information relating to Hellmann’s Healthcare offer, airfreight product solutions and the general Healthcare airfreight industry.
  • Communicate effectively with the network to enhance co-operation.
  • Own and deliver specific projects as assigned by the line manager.
  • Provide progress, status and KPI reports in agreed intervals to the line manager.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position may supervise full-time employees and temporary employees from time to time based on projects.

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree (Business, Logistics and Supply Chain, Transportation, or associate field), or equivalent combination of education and work experience will be considered in lieu of educational requirement.
  • 7-10 years minimum airfreight experience, ideally proven experience in the healthcare and pharmaceutical supply chain and/or healthcare and pharmaceutical customers.
  • 5 years minimum supervisory experience.
  • Completion of any industry related course is an asset.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES

  • Growth mindset
  • Self-starter and proactiveness
  • Results-oriented – drives strategy and execution
  • Knowledge of available active and passive temperature-controlled packaging solutions
  • Good knowledge of GDP related quality system process & procedures, i.e., deviations, CAPA and change control
  • Customer-focused
  • Adaptable and flexible to high-pressure environment
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
  • Analytical skills and problem-solving ability
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Email, and Internet

PHYSICAL DEMANDS

  • Frequently required to stand, and walk
  • Regularly required to sit for extended periods
  • Regularly uses arms to reach, hands and fingers for computer and phone use
  • Speaking clearly and listening for heavy phone contact
  • Requires close-up and computer screen distance vision ability
  • May require occasional overnight travel

Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

The work environment characteristics are similar of those of an office setting with various office equipment.

Inclusion and social diversity are firmly anchored values in our corporate culture. Regardless of gender, age, any disabilities, religion, ethnic origin or sexual identity: We are looking forward to meeting you!

If you are excited by this fantastic opportunity and have what it takes, then click APPLY!

title: Studio Coordinator- Nevada Part Time
description:
OUR PEOPLE POWER OUR PURPOSE

The CorePower team is the heartbeat of the company. We prioritize our people first, and we are invested the employee experience so that together we can create an experience powerful enough to transform lives, including our own. We believe in the power of human connection, community, and going beyond the transactional to make a positive difference in people’s lives. Join our team and discover what happens when you ignite your intention to make a difference.

HOW WE SHOW UP

We are fiercely committed to our core values of empowering everyone, practicing gratitude, building community, growing forward and laughing together. These core values align us in service of CorePower’s higher purpose – to power love from the inside out. They are our guiding principles; internal agreements we make as a CorePower team about how we interact with each other and our students. Living our core values means they guide all our activities, define our workplace culture, and ensure there are no missed opportunities to fulfill our higher purpose.

We embrace our differences and foster an inclusive space where everyone can reach their full potential. We uplift, inspire and guide one another. We make time to share the power of yoga together, celebrate milestones and find joy in the present moment.

ROLE SUMMARY

As a Studio Coordinator (SC), you live your power by supporting the world class CorePower Yoga studio experience including coordinating studio operations and holding the studio to the highest health and safety standards. In alignment with our Core Values, you work alongside the Studio Manager to deliver results and sustained growth towards all current company and studio-level goals. In the SC role, you will learn the business and develop the skillset to operate a studio.

Studio Presence and Guiding the Student Experience

  • Act as an ambassador of the CorePower Yoga Core Values at all times and consistently inspire these values in others
  • Support the Studio Manager in achieving company and studio level goals, including membership growth, retail sales, community outreach, teacher and SET recruitment, and programming enrollment
  • Commit to flexible schedule of 18-29 hours per week in studio in support of operations coordination and teaching (if certified), include health and safety protocol execution, front desk guidance, and team support
  • Must be flexible with schedule availability within the hourly commitment in service of the studio and team
  • Responsibly run the studio, including by acting as the point of contact for students and staff when Studio Manager is not present, up to 20 hours per week
  • Support maintaining an appropriate level of studio supply inventory so that all provisions and amenities are available for students at all times including cleanliness inventory, locker room amenities, towels, programming materials, etc.
  • Engage and know your studio community consistently; greet students by name, serve as an ambassador of yoga both inside and outside of the studio, and spend quality time at the front desk fostering community
  • Support our teachers learning experience of working the POS and other pre/post class duties

Coordinate and Execute Health, Safety and Cleanliness Protocol in the Studio​

  • Uphold high standards for the studio and when on duty, ensure that the physical studio space meets the high CPY standards of cleanliness and functionality including a safe environment, optimum heat and humidity, inspiring music, and clean and clutter-free surroundings in all areas of the studio
  • Support communication around Smart Health Protocol to students upon entry and throughout their visit at CPY ​
  • Act as an extension of the Studio Experience Team (SET) including cleaning the studio, stocking amenities, and ensuring the CPY cleanliness protocol is always followed while on duty in the studio
  • Support the SET team by interviewing SET applicants, hiring SET employees, scheduling SET employee's shifts, stepping in for no call/no shows, training, and disciplining/terminating SET employees who have violated CPY's policies and standards
  • Lead Orientation for new Studio Experience Team members and train them on cleanliness protocol and role expectations

Coordinate Studio Systems

  • Act as a liaison between the Studio Manager and the teaching and SET teams in training, communicating, and coordinating studio operational systems including but not limited to:
  • Point of Sales System (POS); understand and efficiently navigate POS to sign students in, sell packages and memberships, and explore and correct problems with student accounts when at the desk
  • Online Reservation System; support administrative follow up of late cancel fees, waitlist, student support, etc
  • Subbing Application; support training and usage for teaching team
  • HRIS Application; support training and usage for teaching and SET team
  • Help Desk; Submit facilities tickets when on duty ​and communicate follow up needs to Studio Manager

Teaching Schedule

  • Support the studio class schedule by teaching a minimum of 6 classes per week of branded CorePower Yoga classes and support the studio through subbing additional classes as needed

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

HIM Coder II is responsible for coding a variety of services. title: Director of Continuous Improvement
description:
The Director of Continuous Improvement – is responsible for developing and leading a structured continuous improvement strategy across ODL’s global manufacturing sites. This role reports to the EVP, Operations and partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Product Management, Supply Chain leadership to standardize and train associates on how we perform problem solving, value stream mapping, run daily management, and deploy strategy across all ODL sites. The Director will move beyond tools and training—driving behavior change, standardization, accountability, and measurable results that improve delivery, quality, cost, and scalability.

The Impact You’ll Drive

  • Lead continuous improvement and act as a Lean Six Sigma Black Belt facilitator, delivering training and building capability in structured problem solving, continuous improvement, and strategy deployment.
  • Build and execute a multi-year Continuous Improvement (CI) strategy and roadmap aligned to business priorities and operational needs that improves quality, delivery, and cost across all ODL sites leading through influence without having direct authority over site operations.
  • Champion the disciplined use and embedment of Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and structured problem-solving methodologies and tools, enabling teams to identify root causes, implement sustainable countermeasures, and scale best practices across all ODL sites to drive measurable improvements in quality, delivery and cost.
  • Work with ODL Site Leadership to enable our Business Operating System (BOS) across ODL by standardizing our manufacturing processes, documentation, and governance to enable consistent execution and support scalable growth.
  • Drive value stream mapping to identify waste, improve flow, reduce lead time, and enable end-to-end optimization while standardizing and scaling best practices across all ODL sites.
  • Facilitate Kaizen events and Lean transformation initiatives, driving measurable improvements across value streams.
  • Establish and manage CI governance, including project prioritization, resourcing, and validation of financial impact in partnership with Finance.
  • Partner with site leaders to improve key operational metrics including customer PPM, scrap, warranty quality, unit production, inventory, OTIF, and UPLH.
  • Lead change by coaching and developing leaders, building alignment, and embedding continuous improvement into daily management routines across all ODL sites.
  • Foster a culture of accountability, ownership and continuous improvement by identifying, training, and developing CI Champions across the organization.

What sets you up for success:

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain or related field, with 10+ years of experience in manufacturing/operations environments and at least 5 years leading continuous improvement, operational excellence, or transformation initiatives.
  • Lean Six Sigma Black Belt certification
  • Proven track record of driving measurable improvements in cost, quality, delivery, and efficiency, supported by a strong working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and structured problem-solving methodologies.
  • Hands-on experience applying Lean and CI tools (value stream mapping, standard work, 8D, Kaizen) and leveraging manufacturing, tooling, automation, and engineering systems (ERP, PLM) to drive data-informed decisions.
  • Strategic, execution-focused leader who is credible on the floor and in operations & manufacturing spaces, able to influence across functions, communicate clearly, coach at all levels, and sustain improvements beyond short-term wins.
  • Experience in multi-site or global manufacturing networks.
  • Experience implementing and leading enterprise level strategic planning process.
  • Ability to travel (25-50%) to ODL global in the US, Canada, Mexico, UK, & China.

  • Preferred Qualifications
  • BA in Industrial Engineering or related field
  • Master’s Degree
  • Experience in building materials, building products, or similar manufacturing environments.
