title: Senior Reporting Analyst / BI Solutions Specialist
description:
Job Description:

We are looking for a proactive, analytical, and customer-focused Senior Reporting Analyst to lead the design and delivery of high-impact BI solutions. In this role, you will combine deep technical expertise in Power BI and dimensional modeling with a keen interest in modern data engineering practices.


You will serve as a key bridge between internal customers and cloud data engineering teams—translating complex operational challenges and requirements into intuitive, high-performance executive dashboards while optimizing how data flows from the Lakehouse layer into semantic models.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead Requirements Discovery & Advisory:
  • Facilitate discovery workshops with internal customers and cross-functional teams to define KPIs, reporting logic, and dashboard UX wireframes.
  • Confidently advise internal customers on data visualization best practices, cognitive ergonomics, and user-centric analytical design.
  • Architect Robust Semantic Models & Dashboards:
  • Build scalable, high-performance Star Schema models (Fact and Dimension structures) adhering to enterprise modeling standards.
  • Author sophisticated DAX calculations, including complex time-intelligence patterns, dynamic metrics, semi-additive calculations, and Row-Level Security (RLS).
  • Design clean, executive-ready dashboard visualizations that drive actionable decision-making for your internal customers.
  • Optimize Performance & Transformation Placement:
  • Evaluate transformation placement across the entire pipeline (Source vs. Lakehouse vs. Power Query/DAX) to preserve query folding and maximize refresh efficiency.
  • Diagnose and resolve report and visual latency using tools such as Power BI Performance Analyzer, DAX Studio, and VertiPaq Analyzer.
  • Collaborate with Data Engineering:
  • Partner with Data Engineers to shape upstream Lakehouse tables, validate pipeline outputs, and ensure semantic models consistently meet internal customer service-level expectations.

Qualifications & Experience

Essential Experience:

  • 3–5+ years of dedicated, hands-on experience designing and developing enterprise Power BI solutions, semantic data models, and executive dashboards.
  • Expert Dimensional Modeling: Proven ability to build performant Star Schemas from multi-source enterprise environments.
  • Advanced DAX & Power Query (M): Deep expertise writing maintainable DAX measures, implementing dynamic security (RLS/OLS), and leveraging Power Query with full query folding awareness.
  • Transformation Architecture: Clear understanding of where transformations belong across the stack to ensure scalability and cost-efficiency.
  • Customer Engagement & Advisory: Proven experience leading requirements discussions, managing expectations, and presenting analytical insights directly to internal customers and leadership.

Nice to Have (High Advantage):


  • 2+ years of practical experience working with SQL and modern cloud data architectures (e.g., Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake / ADLS Gen2, Snowflake).
  • Databricks Integration: Hands-on experience connecting Power BI to Azure Databricks (Delta tables, Databricks SQL Warehouses) with a solid grasp of storage modes (Import, DirectQuery, and Composite Models).
  • Data Engineering Awareness: Familiarity with Delta Lake concepts/optimizations (e.g., Z-Ordering, Liquid Clustering) and cloud orchestration tools (e.g., Azure Data Factory).

Core Competencies & Mindset


  • Information Passion: Genuine enthusiasm for data storytelling, UI/UX clarity, and empowering internal customers through intuitive visual analytics.
  • Continuous Learner: Strong curiosity to explore upstream data engineering patterns, Lakehouse architectures, and emerging analytics tools.

title: Sr. Production Lead – Peanut M&Ms
description:
Job Description:

Job: Sr. Production Lead – Peanut M&Ms

Shift: B-Shift (Days)

Location: Mars Wrigley Topeka

Mars is looking to hire a Production Leader for our state-of-the-art manufacturing plant in Topeka, Kansas! Being a Mars Associate is all about opportunity. The opportunity to do challenging, exciting work that shapes the world’s best-loved brands. To work with real purpose, supported by talented, friendly people from different backgrounds. Access the tools, training, and experience you need to positively impact our business, the planet, and, most importantly, your career. Being a Mars associate is more than a job. It’s the opportunity to start your day tomorrow.


As part of our overall total compensation package, Mars offers a competitive benefits package to all associates: Medical, Dental, Vision & Life Insurance, Short- & Long-Term Disability, and 401k match. Associates are also immediately eligible (based on hire date) for up to three weeks of vacation, 12 Paid Holidays per year, Sick Pay, Maternity & Parental Leave, and annual bonus earning potential, plus many other ancillary benefits not listed here.

The Production Leader is a shift-based, front-line operations people leader who efficiently improves Quality, Human Safety, and Product Cost Conversion while Engaging and Developing talent. The Production Leaders are responsible for delivering operational targets and leading teams of, on average, 15 production associates. The Production Leader drives safety, quality, continuous improvement, performance management, associate development, team engagement and operating results for their assigned area through shift-based leadership of a line or area that exists within a larger Value Stream organization.


This leader will coordinate the short-term activities of the area within established guidelines and standards to produce the highest quality, lowest cost product most safely and efficiently, while also partnering with the other members of the 24-hour Area Leadership Team to deliver area continuous improvement and Mars Supply Excellence (MSE) program implementation. The Production Leader is responsible for building an effective team on his/her shift and in his/her area of responsibility and for managing the training strategy for both the individual associates and the team. This manager will implement and enforce established policy and area and organizational strategies.


Key Responsibilities:

  • On-the-Job Trainer (OJT) - Obtain and utilize it to deliver and support capability-building programs at the site for Production Leads. Develop and improve Production Lead training/onboarding materials within POKA and teach, coach, assess other leads to level 3 competency. Communicate with Managers about trainee performance and skill gaps, including completion and delivery of the formal hand-off document.
  • Teaching, Coaching and Assess/Expert Trainer – Obtain certification in TCA and Expert Trainer to deliver capability training.
  • Safety and Quality Culture – Set the standard for creating and sustaining a world class safety and quality culture with direct reports and coach peers on how to obtain the standard.
  • Associate Safety – Ensure safe working conditions, behaviors, and mindsets through the direct implementation of Mars Safety programs and driving a relentless focus among a team of operators.
  • Food Safety and Product Quality – Ensure the ongoing production of safe and defect-free products consistent with the principles of Mars. HACCP proficiency is required; this manager owns ongoing training and championing of quality goals and improvements at the Area Shift level.
  • Change Agent - Implement changes in methods, equipment, systems, and organization, as needed, to ensure that the objectives of the line/area are met and give input and recommendations for such changes by using a continuous improvement mindset.
  • Mars Supply Excellence – Lead or participate in one or more MSE Pillars; Lead and support the implementation of Factory Mars Operating System (FMOS), Autonomous Maintenance (AM), and Autonomous Work Teams (AWTs) in area of responsibility (including being a AWT coach and AM cart facilitator); Lead key connection points and own reliability data collection accuracy.
  • Area Ownership – Collaborate with the rest of the Area Leadership Team (Area Manager or Continuous Improvement Engineer, Continuous Improvement Specialist, Maintenance Coordinator) to create and execute the reliability strategy for the area of responsibility.
  • Conversion - Manage the efforts of operating teams of a multi-line, area, or technology on one shift in efficiently converting materials into quality products in a safe, secure, and sanitary manner within the product design specifications.
  • Coaching – Coach operators to build their functional and leadership capabilities and to drive accountability in safety, Quality and Food Safety, Autonomous Maintenance, and team engagement.
  • Line Operations - Coordinate materials, staffing and resources to support line operation and changeovers.
  • Standards Implementation and Adherence – Ensure standards are implemented on shift and in areas of responsibility through effective communication, change management, consistent reinforcement, and coaching, guidance, and accountability measures.
  • Associate Advocacy - Manage associate relations issues and guide and direct the hiring, training, retraining, development, and motivation of Operations associates following self-managed, team-working principles with a minimum degree of guidance from the Area Manager or Value Stream Manager.
  • Engagement - Responsible for facilitating and driving an environment of high associate engagement on the team.
  • Goal Setting and Measurement - With the general guidance of the Value Stream or Area Manager and/or the support of the Continuous Improvement Engineer, establish line and individual performance standards and goals, and measure, control, take corrective action, and report results as appropriate.
  • Troubleshooting – Utilize the technical resources on shift for the preventive maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of process/packaging equipment problems, to effectively use these resources to achieve desired performance levels.
  • Escalations - Proactively identify risks and opportunities and reactively lead on-shift incident resolution when operators require additional support. Prioritize, assign resources against escalated issues, and make decisions to resolve escalated issues.
  • Communications - Ensure that open communications are established and that opportunities to broaden the scope and responsibility of Operations teams/associates are undertaken.
  • Technology Advancement - Advise when opportunities exist for moving the line/area forward in technological change.
  • Operations Strategy - Participate in implementing improvement strategies to help the line/area perform more effectively in the near term.
  • Recruiting and Onboarding – Responsible for partnering with Talent Acquisition to recruit and select associates for operations roles, and responsible for onboarding associates effectively.
  • Associate Development – Develop associates by mentoring and supporting their development plans and helping them grow in functional capability and long-term career;

Job Specifications/Qualifications

Education & Professional Qualification

An undergraduate (Bachelor’s) degree


OR


The equivalent experience is defined as

  • High School Diploma
  • 5 years of experience in a technical manufacturing continuous improvement environment
  • 3 Years of proven high performance in a Production Lead role

Preferred:

  • A degree in one of the Engineering, basic sciences, or business-related disciplines.

Knowledge/Experience:

  • Champion of safety with OSHA experience or certification preferred.
  • Functional knowledge and understanding of HACCP concepts.
  • Working knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practices.
  • Experience in plant sanitation practices and procedures.
  • Proven record of developing talent, engaging associates, and delivering business results
  • Strong understanding of AM and FMOS Fundamentals.
  • Ability to succeed in an ambiguous environment.
  • Ability to deliver critical performance feedback and hold associates accountable to business objectives.
  • Experience and demonstrated capability in leading others.
  • Ability to convey communications clearly and concisely.
  • Understanding of major functions within the plant and the ability to work directly with all levels and functions.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Word, Excel, etc.), internet software, e-mail.



About Mars, Incorporated

Mars is a family-owned business with more than a century of history making diverse products and offering services for people and the pets people love. With almost $35 billion in sales, the company is a global business that produces some of the world’s best-loved brands: M&M’s®, SNICKERS®, TWIX®, MILKY WAY®, DOVE®, PEDIGREE®, ROYAL CANIN®, WHISKAS®, EXTRA®, ORBIT®, 5™, SKITTLES®, UNCLE BEN’S®, MARS DRINKS and COCOAVIA®. Mars also provides veterinary health services that include BANFIELD® Pet Hospitals, Blue Pearl®, VCA® and Pet Partners™. Headquartered in McLean, VA, Mars operates in more than 80 countries. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire its more than 100,000 Associates to create value for all its partners and deliver growth they are proud of every day.

100% Employee-Owned · Big-firm resources, local-team relationships, ONE IMEG culture

Location: Anaheim, CA

Markets: Healthcare; MEP

Travel: Up to 5%

Work Schedule: Full-time in office

Sponsorship: Not available

The records show a strong mechanical and electrical core with plumbing on major projects, plus select structural, civil, technology, and low-voltage support, which suggests a team especially strong in coordinated hospital and technical healthcare systems work.
  • Hospital renovation and expansion, healthcare/research facilities, coordinated inpatient-support and technical building systems, central plant, emergency power, low-voltage, and specialized healthcare infrastructure
  • Recent work includes Huntington Memorial Hospital Renovation & Additions, Healthcare, and Doheny Eye Institute Vision Research Center, Healthcare.

Why IMEG

We put people at the center of who we are, creating positive outcomes for people, communities, and our planet.

  • An assigned mentor to guide your growth from day one

title: Full-Stack Engineer
description:
About the company

Our client is an early-stage AI-native commerce platform building a direct alternative to Shopify and the fragmented legacy commerce stack. The product bundles merchant tools into one system with an AI agent as the primary interface. Founded in 2025, the company has approximately 10 employees, more than 30,000 users, a substantial production codebase, and $7 million in funding.

The role and why it matters

You will join a small, product-led engineering team and own meaningful parts of the platform across the front end and back end. This is a high-agency role for an engineer who wants broad responsibility, works quickly with real customer feedback, and uses AI fluently to increase the speed and quality of delivery.

What you'll do

• Build across the stack and own features from technical design through production launch.

• Treat the front end as a product surface by understanding user behavior and improving the experience, not only implementing designs.

• Design and extend backend systems, APIs, data flows, and integrations that power an AI-native commerce platform.

• Use AI tools as a core part of the development workflow to automate work and accelerate iteration.

• Ship quickly, learn from real users, and improve the product based on direct feedback.

• Work closely with the founders and engineering teammates to make product and technical decisions.

• Take initiative on ambiguous problems without waiting for constant direction.

Requirements

What we're looking for

• 2 or more years of professional experience as a full-stack software engineer.

• Strong ability across both backend and frontend development, with examples of features owned end to end.

• Experience at a high-caliber engineering organization, preferably a venture-backed startup or another product-led, high-growth company.

• Practical fluency with AI development tools and a track record of using them to scale or automate work.

• High agency, strong product sense, and a bias toward action.

• Clear communication and a collaborative approach to feedback and decision-making.

Bonus points

• Experience as a startup founder or early engineer.

• Personal projects or products that demonstrate curiosity and ownership.

• Experience with modern commerce, marketplace, or creator-economy products.

• Experience building AI-native product experiences.

Benefits

Compensation and benefits

• $200K-$250K base salary.

• Competitive equity.

Thornton Tomasetti applies engineering and scientific principles to solve the world’s challenges. Our Protective Design & Security team prioritizes the protection of life and assets by mitigating consequences of security risks in the built environment. With more than 75 years of experience, our risk-led and strategic solutions safeguard people, property, and operations from intentional harm, evolving and emerging threats.


Whether safeguarding a cultural landmark, securing a healthcare facility, or planning for crowd safety at a major event, our approach is grounded in intelligence, simulation, and human-centered design to deliver resilient solutions with demonstrable performance and lasting impact.


Within our practice, you’ll be introduced to how risk-based design brings together security planning, physical security, and electronic security to develop layered protection strategies. You’ll gain exposure to performance-based solutions—from secure site planning to physical hardening, access control, surveillance, and detection—and how these measures integrate with security operations.


Your Role

As an Electronic Security Intern in our Protective Design & Security practice, you will support risk-led security strategies and electronic security design for facilities and campuses across a range of sectors. You will gain exposure to how surveillance, access control, detection, and supporting infrastructure are integrated into the built environment as part of a coordinated, tailored security solution.

title: Project Coordinator
description:
Ledcor Technical Services has been building and servicing communication networks for customers across North America since 1979. Utilizing our broad expertise and experience, we customize solutions to best meet our client's needs. We act as a key partner for our clients by delivering exceptional quality, reliability, and safety in all that we do.

Join our team as a proactive and detail-driven Site Acquisition Coordinator, where you’ll play a key role in managing telecom operations and project performance. This hybrid role blends coordination of field operations with cost tracking and performance analysis, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards. You will collaborate with project managers, engineers, and field teams while also interfacing with clients and stakeholders.

Apply today to become a part of the Ledcor Technical Services team and take the next step in your career!

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and track all phases of telecom site acquisitions including scheduling, materials, access, and closure
  • Maintain and update project logs, QB systems, and Excel trackers to reflect real-time project status
  • Conduct weekly update calls and meetings with internal teams and clients
  • Generate and submit daily work-in-progress (WIP) reports and training summaries
  • Support project cost tracking, including labor, materials, subcontractors, and equipment
  • Assist in preparing cost reports, forecasts, and earned value metrics (CPI, SPI, EAC)
  • Utilize tools like Excel and Power BI to generate performance and status reports
  • Support change management processes and ensure accurate billing and documentation
  • Collaborate with field managers to ensure job readiness and timely project completion
  • Participate in stakeholder meetings and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives

Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with U.S. telecommunications providers and their operational protocols
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, IF Statements, etc.); Power BI and SAP experience is a plus
  • Understanding of project performance metrics such as CPI, SPI, and EAC
  • Experience with Work Breakdown Structures (WBS) and Cost Breakdown Structures (CBS) is an asset
  • Excellent communication and time management skills
  • Ability to work independently and adapt to changing priorities

Work Conditions:

  • This position is a remote position, however the position may be required to travel to the office located in Somerset, KY and/or Florence, KY as needed.

Additional Information

Ledcor Technical Services (LTS) designs, builds, and maintains wireline or wireless networks that span North America and beyond. We are a proven leader and innovator in telecommunications network construction, maintenance, and service installation and repair.

Ledcor has been recognized as a Top 100 Inspiring Workplace in North America.

Our competitive total rewards package provides compensation and benefits that support your physical, mental and financial well-being. We offer exciting, challenging work with opportunities to develop your skills and knowledge.

Employment Equity

At Ledcor we believe diversity, equity, and inclusion should be part of everything we do. We are proud to be an equal-opportunity employer. All qualified individuals, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, Veteran status or any other identifying characteristic are encouraged to apply.

Our True Blue team consists of individuals from all backgrounds who contribute diverse perspectives and experiences to Ledcor. For more information about Ledcor’s Inclusion and Diversity initiatives, please visit our I&D page. Adjustments will be provided in all parts of our hiring process. Applicants need to make their needs known in advance by submitting a request via email.

All applicants must be able to show proof of eligibility to work in the United States.

title: Global Capital Markets - Associate, Strategic Lending Group
location: New York, New York, United States of America
description:
Company Profile

Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries.

As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career - a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.

Divisional Profile

Global Capital Markets (GCM) responds with market judgment and ingenuity to meet clients' needs for capital. Whether executing an IPO, a debt offering or a leveraged buyout, GCM integrates Morgan Stanley's expertise in Sales & Trading and in Investment Banking (IBD), offering clients seamless advice and sophisticated solutions. We originate, structure and execute public and private placement of equities, investment-grade and non-investment-grade debt and related products.

Role Details

  • The Strategic Lending Group (“SLG”) is responsible for the management and origination of a significant corporate loan portfolio and leads the investment committee process for corporate loan requests across Investment Banking and Global Capital Markets. SLG operates at the intersection of deal execution, risk, and strategy. The corporate loans are critical in driving client activity across the integrated investment bank.
  • The Associate will support the evaluation, structuring, approval, and ongoing management of corporate lending transactions and contribute to portfolio strategy initiatives.
  • The role offers exposure to a wide range of financings, including M&A and leveraged buyout commitments and working capital / liquidity facilities, and involves close partnership with stakeholders across IBD, GCM, Sales & Trading, and Credit Risk Management teams.
  • We assist in deal origination / structuring and are responsible for calculating returns, evaluating credit quality, assessing value proposition, optimizing financing structure and terms, and evaluating portfolio strategy and future revenue opportunities.
  • SLG reviews and approves corporate and sponsor financings including M&A and LBO commitments (event loans) as well as working capital / liquidity facilities (relationship loans).
  • The team is looking to hire an Associate who will be based in New York.
  • Deal coverage responsibilities will include:
    • Review lending requests, provide feedback to deal teams and present to investment committee.
    • Interact with senior IBD and GCM management on significant commitment requests.
    • Coordinate with Fixed Income team related to hedge strategy, loan P&L and secondary sales.
    • Work with deal teams to review and execute transactions, including negotiation of loan documentation related to working capital / liquidity facilities.
    • Coordinate with deal teams on challenged loans and drive decisions related to amendments, secondary sales and restructurings.
    • Work with groups across the Firm on the execution of transactions including Credit Risk Management, Operations, Legal, and Treasury.
  • Project Activities include:
    • Provide senior management with regular reporting and analysis related to the portfolio.
    • Ad-hoc projects including conducting large scale data analysis, monitoring market and industry trends, and staying closely aligned with the Firm’s evolving strategic priorities and portfolio objectives
  • Skills Required:
  • Ideally 3+ years of experience within financial sector; experience in Global Capital Markets, Investment Banking, and / or Corporate Finance encouraged.
  • Extraordinarily high level of motivation and commitment to working hard.
  • Extraordinarily high level of focus on work quality and attention to detail.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong client and interpersonal skills.
  • Commercial instinct and effectively prioritize and handle multiple tasks under tight deadlines.
  • Bachelor’s degree is required; must have Regulatory licensing or obtain.

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY:

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices​ into your browser.

Expected base pay rates for the role will be between $150,000 and $225,000 per year for Associate, and $275,000 per year for VP, at the commencement of employment. However, base pay if hired will be determined on an individualized basis and is only part of the total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, incentive compensation, discretionary bonuses, other short and long-term incentive packages, and other Morgan Stanley sponsored benefit programs.

Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents.

Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences.

title: Director, Principal Software Engineer - Strategic Engineering
description:
Use Your Power for Purpose

Technology impacts everything we do. Pfizer’s digital and ‘data first’ strategy is dedicated to implementing innovative and impactful technology solutions across all functions, from research to manufacturing. Whether you are digitizing drug discovery and development, identifying solutions, or making our work easier and faster, you will be making a significant difference to countless lives. By focusing on these advancements, you contribute to a future where technology enhances every aspect of our operations, ultimately benefiting patients worldwide.


What You Will Achieve

In this role, you will focus on code quality, architecture decisions, and reliable delivery while leveraging AI tools to enhance productivity. You will verify and review AI-generated code to ensure it meets our quality standards.


You will be bridging the gap between building products and solving real business problems through rapid solution delivery and deep domain expertise. As part of the discovery-to-scale pipeline, you will identify recurring patterns, and lead validated solutions generalization into enterprise capabilities.


This role encompasses organization-wide technical strategy and architectural direction. You will define strategic direction and be accountable for outcomes, shape organizational practices and maintain external industry visibility. You will handle organizational-scale complexity creating clarity from chaos.


ROLE RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Forward-Deployed Pod Leadership: Lead a forward-deployed pod of engineers and product owners responsible for creating quick, high-quality applications supporting ELT and ELT-1 initiatives
  • Delivery: Drive delivery of the most critical technical initiatives, establish engineering delivery practices across the team, and be the technical authority on high-stakes projects
  • People: Develop technical leaders, shape engineering talent strategy, and build high-performing engineering teams
  • Business: Shape technology-driven strategy, represent technical perspective at executive level, and be recognized as a bridge between engineering and business
  • AI: Design AI-augmented engineering workflows for your area, evaluate new AI tools, train engineers on effective AI usage, and balance speed with verification
  • Reliability: Establish SLOs/SLIs across teams, build resilient systems, lead reliability initiatives for your area, mentor engineers on reliability practices, and drive reliability culture
  • Documentation: Establish documentation standards across teams in your area, build knowledge management systems, and mentor engineers on effective technical writing
  • Process: Drive process efficiency within your team, coordinate cross-functional technical work, and lead retrospectives
  • Executive Communication: Present complex technical solutions to senior leadership and executive audiences in a clear, compelling way
  • Community & Mentorship: Participate as a leader in guild events and serve as an active leader in the mentorship program

ROLE BEHAVIOURS

  • Don't Lose Your Curiosity: Shapes organizational culture around curiosity and continuous learning; sponsors experimental initiatives across the organization; recognized externally as a thought leader in problem discovery; influences industry practices around innovation and exploration
  • Own the Outcome: Defines organizational accountability standards focused on business impact; shapes industry practices around outcome ownership in the AI era; sponsors transformational initiatives with full outcome accountability; recognized externally for ownership culture leadership
  • Be Polymath Oriented: Champions cross-disciplinary learning; creates holistic solutions spanning technical and business domains; embodies the Renaissance Developer ideal; translates specialized knowledge into accessible explanations; thinks like a business insider
  • Communicate with Precision: Creates spec-driven development practices; mentors others on precise communication; spans C-level executives to frontline workers; drives clarity as a core value across their function; represents the organization externally
  • Think in Systems: Shapes systems design practices across their function; conducts chaos engineering experiments; influences cross-team architecture decisions; creates clarity from complexity; bridges technical systems with business processes

EXPERT-LEVEL SKILLS

  • Business Immersion: You are a recognized thought leader. You influence strategy across the business, exemplify the business immersion mindset that defines engineering, and shape how engineering engages with the business.
  • Data Integration: You define data integration patterns and best practices. You architect large-scale data flows, solve the most complex integration challenges, and are the authority on enterprise data integration.
  • Full-Stack Development: You work comfortably in any language and rapidly acquire new skills as needed. You deliver production solutions in days not months, shape full-stack practices and exemplify polymathic engineering.
  • Multi-Audience Communication: You shape communication practices. You represent engineering externally, communicate at board and executive level, and are recognized as an exceptional communicator who bridges any audience gap.
  • Problem Discovery: You shape approaches to problem discovery. You are recognized for transforming ambiguous situations into clear opportunities, influence how teams engage with business problems, and are the go-to person for the most undefined challenges.
  • Rapid Prototyping & Validation: You shape culture around rapid validation and iterative delivery. You are recognized for transformative fast delivery, define standards for prototype-to-production, and exemplify the "deliver in days" mindset.
  • Stakeholder Management: You shape stakeholder practices. You manage executive relationships, represent engineering at the highest levels, and are recognized for exceptional stakeholder partnerships.
  • Team Collaboration: You create collaborative culture. You transform dysfunctional team dynamics, are recognized for building exceptional teams, and mentor others on collaboration excellence.

PRACTITIONER-LEVEL SKILLS

  • AI Evaluation & Verification: You lead AI governance initiatives across teams in your area, create evaluation standards and checklists, and train engineers on rigorous AI verification. You design review processes for AI-assisted work.
  • AI Literacy: You guide AI adoption decisions across teams in your area, assess AI risks and benefits systematically, and train engineers on responsible AI usage. You design human-in-the-loop workflows.
  • AI-Augmented Development: You optimize AI tool usage across teams in your area, train engineers on AI-augmented workflows, evaluate new AI development tools, and establish practices that balance AI speed with verification rigor.
  • Architecture & Design: You design complex multi-component systems end-to-end, evaluate architectural options for large initiatives across teams, guide technical decisions for your area, and mentor engineers on architecture. You balance elegance with delivery needs.
  • Code Quality & Review: You establish and enforce quality standards across teams in your area. You mentor engineers on effective code review, ensure verification depth for AI-assisted development, and drive testing strategies.
  • Developer Experience: You lead developer experience initiatives across teams in your area. You design comprehensive self-service platforms, establish DX metrics, conduct systematic user research, and mentor engineers on platform-as-product thinking.
  • Knowledge Management: You lead knowledge management initiatives across teams in your area, create knowledge systems and taxonomies, establish practices that make institutional knowledge persistent, and mentor others on knowledge sharing.
  • Pattern Generalization: You lead pattern generalization initiatives across teams, define criteria for when to generalize vs keep custom. You mentor engineers on abstraction design.
  • Service Management: You lead service management practices for multiple services across teams, optimize service portfolios for your area, balance service investments, and train engineers on service-oriented thinking.
  • Site Reliability Engineering: You define reliability standards across teams in your area, drive post-incident improvements systematically, design capacity planning processes, and mentor engineers on SRE practices.
  • Technical Writing: You define documentation standards across teams in your area, create documentation systems and templates, train engineers on spec-driven development, and ensure documentation quality across projects.

WORKING-LEVEL SKILLS

  • Cloud Platforms: You design cloud-native solutions, manage infrastructure as code, implement security best practices, and make informed service selections. You troubleshoot cloud-specific issues.
  • Data Modeling: You create efficient data models that balance normalization with query performance. You optimize queries, handle schema migrations safely, and choose appropriate storage technologies.
  • DevOps & CI/CD: You build complete CI/CD pipelines end-to-end, manage infrastructure as code (Terraform, CloudFormation), implement monitoring, and design deployment strategies for your services.
  • Lean Thinking & Flow: You optimize team processes systematically, measure and improve cycle time, remove bottlenecks proactively, and deliver rapidly while maintaining quality.
  • Technical Debt Management: You prioritize debt systematically based on risk and impact, balance debt reduction with feature work, and make pragmatic trade-offs. You know when to take on debt intentionally.
  • Time Management & Deep Work: You protect focused time for complex work, balance multiple priorities without dropping balls, minimize context switching, and help others understand your capacity.

Here Is What You Need (Minimum Requirements)

  • Applicant must have a bachelor's degree, in Computer Science, Engineering or related field preferred, with at least 8 years of​ experience; OR a master's degree with at least 7 years of experience; OR​ a PhD with 5+ years of experience​
  • Demonstrated track record of having personally created applications that are actively used with senior leadership (ELT / ELT-1), with the ability to present complex technical solutions to executive audiences
  • Candidate demonstrates a breadth of diverse leadership experiences and capabilities including: the ability to influence and collaborate with peers, develop and coach others, oversee and guide the work of other colleagues to achieve meaningful outcomes and create business impact.

PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

Extended Laptop and Desk time throughout the workday


NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS

25% required travel


Work Location Assignment: Hybrid


Last Date to Apply: September 30, 2026

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $176,600.00 to $294,300.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 20.0% of the base salary and eligibility to participate in our share based long term incentive program. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. title: Infectious Disease Specialist
description:
Position Title: Infectious Disease Specialist - Per Diem

Department of Medicine, Division of Infectious Diseases

HMFP at BIDMC

Harvard Medical School

The Medicine Department at HMFP @ BIDMC is seeking an Infectious Disease Specialist for a per diem position. Your duties will include ad hoc weekend inpatient coverage. Your primary location will be BID-Needham. However, from time to time, based on clinical need, we may additionally arrange for you to provide services at other locations or within other affiliated entities.


Job Requirements (examples below)

  • MD or DO from an accredited medical school
  • Board-certified or eligible in Infectious Diseases
  • A valid MA medical license or the ability to obtain one
  • Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment

The department will be engaged in the newly announced and exciting clinical collaboration between Dana-Farber Cancer Institute (DFCI), BIDMC, and Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians (HMFP) to establish New England’s only free-standing adult inpatient cancer hospital. The collaboration will bring together world-class clinicians to deliver transformational, precision medicine in an environment solely dedicated to defying cancer.

Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, a 743-bed hospital and Level 1 Trauma Center, is a founding member of Beth Israel Lahey Health (BILH). BILH, a health care system with 14 hospitals, brings together academic medical centers and teaching hospitals, community and specialty hospitals, and more than 4,000 physicians and 39,000 employees in a shared mission to expand access and advance the science and practice of medicine through groundbreaking research and education.

Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (HMFP) is one of the largest physician organizations in New England, dedicated to excellence and innovation in patient care, education, and research. As a physician-led organization, HMFP partners with more than 2,400 providers to support the delivery of exceptional care, promote professional development and foster balance at work and home. HMFP physicians have faculty affiliations with Harvard Medical School (HMS) and provide care throughout BILH system and additional hospitals across Massachusetts.

For information about the position, please contact Brett Rubin: brubin@bidmc.harvard.edu. Candidates should apply directly to Workday.

description:

Job Description Summary

We are seeking a highly motivated Senior Scientist to join the Exploratory Chemical Biology team within the Novartis Biomedical Research in San Diego. The successful candidate will contribute to the discovery of LMW, peptide, and protein therapeutics through the application of modern display technologies and molecular engineering approaches.

This position provides a unique opportunity to work at the interface of chemical biology, protein engineering, and emerging therapeutic modalities. The successful candidate will support discovery programs through the design and execution of display selections, library constructions, molecular characterizations, and data analyses in a highly collaborative research environment.


Job Description

Internal Job Title: Senior Scientist I/II

Position Location: onsite, San Diego, CA

Bring your expertise in display technologies and molecular engineering to one of the industry's most innovative research organizations. As a Senior Scientist in Exploratory Chemical Biology at Novartis Biomedical Research, you will help unlock new therapeutic possibilities across small molecules, peptides, and proteins. You'll collaborate with world-class scientists, apply emerging discovery technologies, and contribute to building next-generation platforms that enable breakthrough medicines. If you thrive in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment and are excited by scientific innovation, this role offers an exceptional opportunity to make a meaningful impact on how future medicines are discovered.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and execute peptide and protein discovery campaigns using phage, mRNA, yeast, and other display or selection platforms.

  • Generate, characterize, and quality-control combinatorial libraries using cloning, PCR, DNA assembly, mutagenesis, and sequencing.

  • Identify and optimize discovery candidates through iterative selection, molecular engineering, and biochemical or biophysical characterization using ELISA, flow cytometry, BLI, SPR, and related technologies.

  • Analyze data and clearly communicate findings to project teams.

  • Implement new technologies, workflows, and automation approaches to improve discovery efficiency.

Essential Requirements:

  • BS, MS, or recent PhD (within last 2 years) in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Chemical Biology, Bioengineering, or a related field, with 4+ years of relevant experience or training. Drug discovery experience preferred.

  • Hands-on experience with display technologies (phage, yeast, and/or mRNA), screening and assay technologies, and molecular biology methods, including library construction and quality control, PCR, cloning, electroporation, and DNA assembly.

  • Strong laboratory skills, attention to experimental detail, and accurate, timely documentation in electronic laboratory notebooks.

  • Strong organizational and prioritization skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deliver results within established timelines.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with a demonstrated ability to work effectively in a diverse, collaborative team.

What sets us apart is how we work. We back bold thinking, move with pace, and turn ideas into action. You’ll have the opportunity to make a real impact across your team, the business, and for the clients we support every day.

HUB24 Limited is an ASX-listed company (ASX: HUB) and part of the ASX100. We have over 1,100 employees across Australia, with offices in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane, Perth and the Gold Coast.


Why you’ll enjoy working here


We create an environment where you can do your best work and see the impact of it.

  • Work with smart, collaborative people who get things done.

Why this is an exciting opportunity


The Senior DevOps Engineer is a senior technical specialist responsible for designing, implementing, automating, and continuously improving cloud platforms, infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, observability solutions, and operational excellence practices. This role partners closely with Platform, Cyber Security, Software Engineering, Product, and Test teams to deliver secure, scalable, reliable, and highly available technology solutions. The position provides technical leadership, drives DevOps maturity, and champions automation, innovation, and engineering best practices across the organisation.

What you’ll be doing


Cloud & Platform Engineering
  • Design, implement, and maintain scalable cloud platforms across AWS and/or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives and promote engineering excellence across the organisation.


What you bring

Experience & Skills


  • Minimum 7 years' experience in DevOps, Cloud Engineering, Platform Engineering, or related disciplines.
  • Proven experience operating and supporting enterprise-scale cloud environments.

  • Experience leading cloud migration, platform transformation, or modernization initiatives.
  • Experience supporting business-critical production systems in high-availability environments.
  • Experience working within Agile delivery frameworks.
  • Relevant certifications such as AWS Solutions Architect, AWS DevOps Engineer, Kubernetes, or Terraform are highly desirable.

Leadership & Communication


  • Strong stakeholder engagement and relationship management skills.
  • Ability to influence technical direction and engineering standards.
  • Proven mentoring and coaching capability.
  • Excellent verbal, written, documentation, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to lead technical initiatives across multiple teams and functions.

title: MEP/Carpentry Foreman
description:
Position Overview

We are seeking an experienced Working Foreman to join our commercial construction team. This is a hands-on leadership position for someone with a strong background in commercial tenant improvement and/or ground-up construction who can effectively coordinate crews, communicate with other trades, maintain jobsite safety, and assist the Superintendent with daily project documentation.

The ideal candidate will have a background as a Plumbing, Electrical, Carpentry, or General Construction Foreman and possess a solid understanding of how multiple trades coordinate on a commercial jobsite. Carpentry experience is highly valuable, particularly for candidates who are comfortable reading plans and working through construction details.

This position will initially support an active commercial project and will transition to a ground-up medical office building project.

Key Responsibilities

  • Coordinate daily with other Foremen to review jobsite safety, manpower, scheduling, and project progress
  • Lead and work alongside a crew while maintaining productivity and quality standards
  • Assist the Superintendent with daily paperwork, documentation, and project reporting
  • Complete daily jobsite entries and maintain accurate records of work performed
  • Take and organize daily progress photos for each subcontractor/trade
  • Monitor jobsite progress and communicate potential issues or delays to the Superintendent
  • Coordinate work between various trades to help maintain an efficient workflow
  • Maintain a safe, clean, and organized jobsite
  • Perform hands-on construction work alongside the crew, including minor detail/finish work and cleanup
  • Help ensure work is completed according to plans, specifications, quality standards, and project schedule
  • Read and interpret construction plans and drawings when necessary
  • Identify potential conflicts between trades and communicate issues proactively
  • Assist with maintaining project schedules and coordinating upcoming work
  • Support the Superintendent with general field operations and jobsite coordination
  • Ensure crews follow company and project-specific safety requirements

Project Background

The successful candidate will have experience working on commercial construction projects, particularly:

  • Commercial Tenant Improvements (TI)
  • Ground-up commercial construction
  • Medical office or healthcare construction is a plus
  • Multi-trade commercial projects
  • Projects involving significant MEP coordination

Requirements

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate will have:

  • 3+ years of commercial construction experience
  • Previous experience as a Foreman, Working Foreman, Lead, or similar field leadership role
  • Experience with commercial tenant improvement and/or ground-up construction
  • Background with a plumbing, electrical, carpentry, or other commercial construction subcontractor
  • Working knowledge of MEP systems and trade coordination
  • Strong understanding of commercial construction sequencing
  • Ability to read and understand construction plans is highly preferred
  • Strong communication and organizational skills
  • Ability to coordinate effectively with other Foremen, subcontractors, and the Superintendent
  • Ability to work with a crew while also performing hands-on construction work
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Ability to learn new construction processes, plans, and project requirements quickly
  • Reliable transportation and ability to work on an active commercial jobsite

What We're Looking For

This is not a strictly supervisory Foreman position. The successful candidate should be comfortable working alongside their crew, jumping in on minor detail work, helping with cleanup, and assisting wherever needed to keep the project moving.

We are looking for someone who can combine hands-on construction skills with field leadership and coordination — someone who can communicate with other Foremen and the Superintendent, understand what needs to happen next, and help make sure the work gets done correctly and safely.

Commercial tenant improvement or ground-up construction experience is strongly preferred.

title: Media Relations Coordinator
description:
If you are a current University of Tampa student, please search for and apply to student jobs here via Workday. Job applications for current students will not be considered if submitted through the external career center.

Position Details

The Media Relations Coordinator supports the University of Tampa’s external visibility and reputation by serving as the day-to-day point of contact for media relations. The coordinator works proactively and responsively with journalists, faculty, staff and University leaders to identify and develop media opportunities, connect reporters with University experts, and help position UTampa faculty and programs as authoritative sources on issues of public interest.

Reporting to the Director of Institutional Marketing and Content Strategy, the coordinator also works closely with the University’s external public relations agency and colleagues across Marketing and Communications to advance institutional priorities, faculty thought leadership and the University’s broader reputation.


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Serve as a primary day-to-day contact for journalists and media inquiries, coordinating timely responses and connecting reporters with appropriate University experts and spokespeople.
  • Develop and maintain productive relationships with local, regional and national journalists, editors, producers and other media contacts.
  • Proactively identify, develop and pitch stories that showcase UTampa faculty expertise, academic programs, research, student experiences and institutional priorities.
  • Work directly with faculty and staff to identify areas of expertise and develop opportunities for media commentary, interviews, contributed content and thought leadership.
  • Monitor news cycles and emerging issues to identify timely opportunities for University experts to contribute perspective and analysis.
  • Prepare faculty, staff and University leaders for media interviews, including background information, key messages, anticipated questions and interview guidance.
  • Draft and edit media materials including pitches, media advisories, press releases, statements, talking points, briefing materials and other external communications.
  • Coordinate the day-to-day relationship with the University’s external public relations agency, including sharing priorities, identifying opportunities, facilitating access to faculty and institutional experts, and supporting execution of media initiatives. Strategic direction, priorities and agency accountability remain with the director.
  • Track earned media activity, placements, journalist engagement and other media relations outcomes and contribute to regular reporting and analysis.
  • Monitor media coverage involving the University, its leadership, faculty, programs and issues affecting higher education and the Tampa Bay region.
  • Support communications related to emerging or sensitive issues by gathering information, coordinating media inquiries and assisting with messaging and response materials under the direction of senior leadership.
  • Support major institutional announcements, awards, recognitions and other select public relations initiatives that strengthen University visibility and reputation.
  • Collaborate with writers, content strategists, social media, creative and digital colleagues to extend earned media opportunities across University-owned channels when appropriate.
  • Maintain media lists, faculty expert information and other media relations resources.
  • Perform other duties related to media relations, reputation and external communications as assigned.

Qualifications

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in communications, journalism, public relations, marketing or a related field.
  • Three to five years of professional experience in media relations, public relations, journalism, communications or a closely related field.
  • Demonstrated experience working with journalists and responding to media inquiries.
  • Strong writing, editing and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to identify compelling stories and translate complex or specialized information into clear, accessible narratives.
  • Experience developing media pitches, press releases, briefing materials or similar communications.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines in a fast-moving environment.
  • Sound judgment, professionalism and discretion when working with sensitive or time-sensitive information.
  • Ability to build productive relationships with faculty, staff, journalists and external partners.

Preferred

  • Experience in higher education, a complex organization, agency public relations, journalism or a related environment.
  • Experience supporting faculty experts, executives or other subject-matter experts in media interviews.
  • Familiarity with media monitoring, media databases and earned media measurement tools.
  • Experience supporting thought leadership or proactive reputation-building campaigns.

Work Schedule
Monday through Friday from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.
Summer: Monday through Thursday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m.

The University of Tampa offers great benefits, including:

  • Free Tuition

  • 100% Employer-Funded Health Reimbursement Account
  • 100% Employer-Paid Short & Long Term Disability Insurance
  • 100% Employer-Funded Employee Assistance Program

  • Free On-Campus Parking
  • Access to Campus Amenities (pool, library, campus events, and more)
  • Fitness Center

  • Flexible Spending Accounts

title: Senior Operations Associate- Lab Equipment Management
location: United States - New York - Pearl River
description:
Job Description

Why Patients Need You

Pfizer’s purpose is to deliver breakthroughs that change patients’ lives. Research and Development is at the heart of fulfilling Pfizer’s purpose as we work to translate advanced science and technologies into the therapies and vaccines that matter most. Whether you are in the discovery sciences, ensuring drug safety and efficacy or supporting clinical trials, you will apply cutting edge design and process development capabilities to accelerate and bring the best in class medicines to patients around the world.

What You Will Achieve

This position is primarily responsible for business operations support of the Electronic Chart Recorder (ECR) & Electronic Monitoring Systems (EMS), i.e., Honeywell & ANS -Siemens/ systems for laboratory-based groups within Vaccines located in Pearl River.

This individual will be the single point of contact for identifying and notifying the correct resources in order to keep equipment within the lab running optimally. This involves work with multiple stakeholders including: Vaccines colleagues, managers & Leadership Team, Quality, Informatics & Data Operations (QIDO), Global Workplace Experience (GWE), Pfizer Digital, Compass, Site Services, Procurement, and outside vendors.


How You Will Achieve It

  • Serve as the single point-of-contact for lab-based groups totaling over 500 colleagues, creating, maintaining, and updating system users’ profiles and responder lists.
  • Reconcile requests for new responder lists with possibly existing lists.
  • Provide screenshots of EMS related deliverables to verify change request. Provide trend data for LDRs or general inquiry.
  • Regularly review and verify usernames and emails to coordinate with any organizational changes, colleague moves or retirements.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for onboarding new chambers to the Honeywell monitoring system, including providing guidance on ECR/EMS connectivity requirements, and reviewing LAMMS request submissions for accuracy and completeness prior to Honeywell implementation activities.
  • Serve as point person for existing chamber moves within and between laboratories. Provide support/ guidance on steps to disconnect & reconnect existing chambers to the ECR/EMS systems
  • Serve as the LAMMS (Laboratory Asset Monitoring and Management System) power user, providing guidance and support to stakeholders, facilitating system requests, and representing laboratory operations in enhancement discussions and future system development initiatives.
  • Maintain the configuration and responder list files within LAMMS. Process ECR account requests as well as annually recertify accounts. Reset password requests.
  • Troubleshoot aberrant alarms, issues with notification receipts (calls/texts/emails) and associated root causes as requested by lab colleagues. Collaborate with GWE/ Vaccines Operations/ Procurement to determine if a replacement chamber is warranted.
  • Work efficiently as part of a Laboratory support team in a matrixed environment.
  • Know and model Pfizer Values and Pfizer Core Competencies



Qualifications

Must-Have

  • BS with 3+ years of relevant experience or MS with at least 1+ years relevant laboratory experience
  • Experience with laboratory equipment management.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and must be motivated, flexible, highly organized, and willing to learn new skill sets.
  • Strong oral and written communication skills.
  • Strong computer skills – must be proficient in Microsoft Office.
  • Experience working with groups such as Vaccines Quality, Informatics & Data Operations Amentum, Global Workforce Experience, and demonstrated ability to bridge laboratory needs with internal and external services to meet those needs.
  • Experience preparing, reviewing, and managing GMP-controlled documentation, including SOPs, LDRs, CCRs, and equipment qualification documentation (e.g., IQ/OQ protocols, reports, and supporting records).

Nice-to-Have

  • Hands on Experience with LAMMS, EAMS (Enterprise Asset Management System), Honeywell & ANS (Automatic Notification System) Response.

PHYSICAL/MENTAL REQUIREMENTS

  • Standard office environment, with the individual co-located in open space or workstation with other staff and scientists.
  • Access to laboratory which will require appropriate Environmental Health and Safety training be completed.
  • No significant physical requirements except significant amounts of computer/keyboard use.

NON-STANDARD WORK SCHEDULE, TRAVEL OR ENVIRONMENT REQUIREMENTS


Occasional travel may be required to engage with peers at other VRD sites or outside vendors

Work Location Assignment: This is a hybrid role requiring you to live within commuting distance and work on-site an average of 2.5 days per week or more as needed.

Last Day to Apply: September 29, 2026

The annual base salary for this position ranges from $79,400.00 to $132,400.00. In addition, this position is eligible for participation in Pfizer’s Global Performance Plan with a bonus target of 7.5% of the base salary. We offer comprehensive and generous benefits and programs to help our colleagues lead healthy lives and to support each of life’s moments. Benefits offered include a 401(k) plan with Pfizer Matching Contributions and an additional Pfizer Retirement Savings Contribution, paid vacation, holiday and personal days, paid caregiver/parental and medical leave, and health benefits to include medical, prescription drug, dental and vision coverage. Learn more at Pfizer Candidate Site – U.S. Benefits | (uscandidates.mypfizerbenefits.com). Pfizer compensation structures and benefit packages are aligned based on the location of hire. The United States salary range provided does not apply to Tampa, FL or any location outside of the United States.

Relocation assistance may be available based on business needs and/or eligibility.

Candidates must be authorized to be employed in the U.S. by any employer.

U.S. work visa sponsorship (such as TN, O-1, H-1B, etc.) is not available for this role now or in the future.

Sunshine Act

Pfizer reports payments and other transfers of value to health care providers as required by federal and state transparency laws and implementing regulations. These laws and regulations require Pfizer to provide government agencies with information such as a health care provider’s name, address and the type of payments or other value received, generally for public disclosure. Subject to further legal review and statutory or regulatory clarification, which Pfizer intends to pursue, reimbursement of recruiting expenses for licensed physicians may constitute a reportable transfer of value under the federal transparency law commonly known as the Sunshine Act. Therefore, if you are a licensed physician who incurs recruiting expenses as a result of interviewing with Pfizer that we pay or reimburse, your name, address and the amount of payments made currently will be reported to the government. title: Sr. Engineering Technician
description:
Lyten is leading an industrial revolution through Lyten 3D Graphene™, a breakthrough supermaterial unlocking a new generation of products — from lithium–sulfur batteries and energy storage systems to concrete admixtures, lightweight composites, and next-generation sensors that are revolutionizing industries. Together, these innovations are making a massive global improvement and driving real-world impact across energy, mobility, construction, and defense.

At Lyten, we believe the most meaningful careers begin with purpose — and with people who want to make a difference. We’re not just developing advanced supermaterials — we’re about to change the world as we know it, reshaping how energy is stored, how products are built, and how progress is made.

We’re entering an exciting growth phase, scaling production across the U.S. and Europe and expanding our team of engineers, scientists, and innovators.

Apply now to join our team and be part of something bigger than yourself — where collaboration, creativity, and purpose come together to build the technologies that will define the next century.


Sr. Engineering Technician

We are seeking a hands-on Sr. Engineering Technician to support the development, optimization, and daily operation of our battery electrode manufacturing line. Working closely with Process Engineers and R&D, you will execute experimental runs, operate pilot-scale equipment, maintain strict quality control, and troubleshoot real-time production issues to ensure high process yield and consistency.

Key Responsibilities

  • Equipment Operation: Set up, operate, and maintain pilot-scale electrode manufacturing equipment, including planetary/high-shear mixers, slot-die coaters, and calender.
  • Process Execution: Execute Design of Experiments (DOE) trials and routine production runs under the direction of process engineers, carefully tracking critical process parameters.
  • Quality & Metrology: Conduct in-line and offline measurements (e.g., slurry viscosity/rheology, coating thickness, mass loading, particle size analysis) to monitor product quality and statistical process control.
  • Troubleshooting & Maintenance: Act as frontline technical support to identify, document, and resolve real-time process defects and mechanical issues to minimize line downtime.
  • Documentation: Draft and update Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), batch records, build logs, and maintenance checklists with high attention to detail.
  • Cross-Functional Support: Collaborate with R&D, Quality, and Manufacturing teams to support process scaling from lab-scale prototypes to full production lines.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in related field (e.g., engineering, chemistry, experimental physics) and 2+ years of relevant experience OR Bachelor's degree (unrelated field) AND 5+ years of experience in R&D or low volume manufacturing OR 1+ years of experience with significant responsibilities at a high-volume cell manufacturing facility (e.g., PENA or Tesla) OR Associate's degree in related field (engineering, chemistry, experimental physics) AND 4+ years of relevant experience OR Associate's degree (unrelated field) AND 6+ years of experience in R&D or low volume manufacturing OR 2+ years of experience with significant responsibilities at a high volume cell manufacturing facility (e.g., PENA or Tesla)
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and practical problem-solving skills for real-time equipment troubleshooting.
  • Familiarity with standard lab and measurement tools (e.g., micrometers, viscometers, balances, optical microscopes).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Basic proficiency with data entry and analysis tools (Excel, JMP, or manufacturing execution systems).
  • Experience assisting with materials characterization (e.g., SEM, XRD, PSA).
  • Prior involvement in equipment installation, startup, or scale-up activities.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment and lift up to 35 lbs. as required by daily operations.

Compensations Range:

The expected base salary range for this position is between

$42.12 - $63.17

The level of pay within the range will depend on a variety of job-related factors that may include location, relevant prior experience and/or education, or particular skills and expertise.

This compensation and benefits information is based on Lyten’s estimate as of the date of publication and may be modified in the future. We generally do not negotiate on salary once we have made an offer. The level of pay within the range will depend on a variety of job-related factors that may include location, relevant prior experience and/or education, or particular skills and expertise. Why Work at Lyten

At Lyten, you’ll be part of a team that’s redefining what’s possible in energy, materials, and manufacturing. We’re not just imagining the future — we’re building it today with breakthrough technologies that are changing how products are made and how industries innovate.

Our people are the heart of that mission. From world-class scientists and engineers to creative problem-solvers in operations, manufacturing, and commercialization, every member of the Lyten team plays a role in turning bold ideas into real-world impact. We believe that the best work happens when you’re doing great things in the world — with people you like. Collaboration, curiosity, and a shared sense of purpose drive everything we do.

What You’ll Find at Lyten

  • A mission that matters: Contribute directly to solving complex challenges in energy, mobility, and materials innovation.

  • Cutting-edge innovation: Work on technologies at the intersection of materials science, energy storage, and advanced manufacturing that strengthen energy security and local supply chains.

  • Extraordinary people: Join a team of talented, friendly, and down-to-earth innovators who support, challenge, and inspire one another every day.

  • Teamwork and culture: Experience a workplace built on trust, respect, and shared success — where collaboration fuels breakthroughs and everyone’s ideas are heard.

  • Global impact: Help scale new materials and energy solutions that reinforce industrial resilience across the U.S. and Europe.

  • Career growth: Be part of a fast-moving company entering a commercial growth phase, with opportunities to lead, learn, and make your mark.

  • Purpose-driven values: Thrive in an environment that celebrates ingenuity, optimism, and meaningful progress — together.

Lyten offers the opportunity to do the most important work of your career — helping build the technologies that will power the next century of innovation.

Join us, and help transform industries, communities, and the planet with friends who share your drive to make a difference.

description:
About Us:


Morgan Stanley (“MS”) is a global financial services firm that conducts its business through three principal business segments—Institutional Securities, Wealth Management (WM), and Asset Management. Morgan Stanley provides comprehensive financial advice and services to its clients including brokerage, investment advisory, financial and wealth planning, credit and lending, deposits and cash management, annuities, insurance, retirement, and trust services. The WM and U.S. Banks Financial Crimes Risk Assistant Vice President (AVP) is part of Wealth Management and the Morgan Stanley Private Bank, National Association and the Morgan Stanley Bank, NA (collectively, the “U.S. Banks”) on the WM and U.S. Banks Financial Crimes Risk Team.

As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in doing the right thing, putting clients first, leading with exceptional ideas and a commitment to diversity and inclusion. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career – a place for people to learn, achieve, and grow.

Department Profile:


The WM and U.S. Banks Financial Crimes Risk Team is embedded within the Firm’s business line. It is responsible for identifying, assessing, and escalating potential money laundering and reputational risk issues associated with higher risk client types. The WM and U.S. Banks Financial Crimes Risk Team is considered the first line of defense and supports the onboarding, enhanced due diligence, and negative news processes for Morgan Stanley.

Responsibilities:


The First Line Financial Crime EDD Associate will be responsible for executing risk-relevant activities related to AML. The First Line Financial Crime EDD Associate will assess Bank Secrecy Act (BSA), money laundering and reputational risk matters identified through the execution of the Firm’s EDD protocols and will have ultimate responsibility for the escalation of issues or risks related to these processes. Additionally, this role is expected to periodically support ad-hoc projects and initiatives, including remediation lookbacks and/or root-cause analysis and solutions implementation.

The First Line Financial Crime EDD Team Associate will:

  • Review documents and information to perform enhanced due diligence reviews on higher risk customers
  • Act as key support for ad-hoc remediation projects and initiatives related to assessing and mitigating the Firm’s exposure to money laundering and reputational risk-relevant activities.
  • Develop broad knowledge of the EDD review operations end-to-end cycle and provide subject matter guidance to project teams
  • Ensure timely feedback loop on identified gaps or issues to stakeholders involved in EDD operations
  • Actively identify, measure, control and remediate AML and reputational risk issues with partners in Global Financial Crimes, Compliance, and the Business Units
  • Perform processes in accordance with internal policies, develop and monitor periodic AML reporting to senior stakeholders, and make recommendations to improve procedures governing AML-related activities
  • Active pipeline management and engagement with Financial Advisors, Complex Management and Risk Officers to manage client relationships
  • Collaborate with Global Financial Crimes to ensure the BSA/AML program operates effectively and continues to comply with regulatory requirements and expectations

Required Experience:

  • Have 3-6 years of relevant experience with BSA/AML Regulations within the financial services industry, or at a financial services regulator (e.g., FINRA, Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, Federal Reserve Bank, Securities and Exchange Commission, etc.)
  • Have a bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or other related field
  • Strong knowledge of Know Your Customer, Customer Identification Program and CDD requirements
  • Strong interpersonal skills and ability to communicate effectively both verbally and in writing
  • Strong work ethic with an ability to work both independently and with team members, under tight deadlines
  • Ability to work in a high volume, fast paced environment
  • Ability to handle highly confidential information professionally and with appropriate discretion

Skills Desired:

  • Working knowledge of MS Office
  • Certified as an Anti-Money Laundering Specialist by ACAMS or equivalent AML certification/license is a plus

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY:

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry.
