title: Plant Tissue Culture Technician
description:
We are seeking an experienced Plant Tissue Culture Technician responsible for the laboratory-based propagation of rare, endangered, difficult-to-propagate, and high-value plant species using tissue culture and micropropagation techniques.

The role will support living plant collections, plant conservation programmes, and specialised in-vitro propagation activities. The successful candidate will establish and maintain sterile laboratory conditions, prepare culture media, initiate and maintain plant cultures, monitor plant development, and support the acclimatisation of tissue-cultured plants.

Key Responsibilities

  • Propagate rare, endangered, difficult-to-propagate, and high-value plant species using tissue culture and micropropagation techniques.
  • Initiate, establish, multiply, root, and maintain in-vitro plant cultures according to species-specific protocols.
  • Select and prepare suitable explant material for tissue culture initiation.
  • Perform surface sterilisation and maintain strict aseptic techniques to minimise contamination.
  • Prepare and modify plant tissue culture media, including nutrients, vitamins, plant growth regulators, carbohydrates, and gelling agents.
  • Monitor cultures for growth, development, contamination, physiological abnormalities, and overall performance.
  • Conduct routine subculturing and transfer plant material under sterile conditions.
  • Maintain appropriate temperature, photoperiod, light intensity, and other environmental conditions for tissue cultures.
  • Operate, clean, sterilise, and maintain laboratory equipment including autoclaves, laminar-flow cabinets, growth chambers, balances, pH meters, and microscopes.
  • Monitor equipment performance and coordinate maintenance and calibration requirements.
  • Implement laboratory cleaning, sterilisation, contamination-control, and waste-management procedures.
  • Identify sources of microbial contamination and implement corrective and preventive measures.
  • Support the transfer and acclimatisation of tissue-cultured plants from in-vitro to ex-vitro conditions.
  • Develop, refine, document, and standardise tissue culture protocols for priority plant species.
  • Maintain detailed records covering explant sources, media formulations, culture dates, subcultures, treatments, contamination rates, multiplication rates, rooting success, and plant survival.
  • Maintain laboratory inventories of culture media components, consumables, chemicals, glassware, and sterile materials.
  • Support plant conservation and recovery programmes for endangered, threatened, rare, and difficult-to-propagate species.
  • Assist with research and trials aimed at improving propagation success.
  • Provide practical training and technical guidance to staff, interns, and students.
  • Ensure laboratory activities comply with applicable health, safety, chemical handling, biological material, biosecurity, and laboratory operating requirements.

Requirements

  • Degree in Biology, Plant Biology, Botany, Biotechnology, Plant Sciences, Horticulture, or a related field.
  • Formal training in plant tissue culture, micropropagation, plant biotechnology, or related laboratory techniques is preferred.
  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant laboratory experience involving plant tissue culture and micropropagation.
  • Demonstrated practical experience in culture initiation, multiplication, subculturing, rooting, and culture maintenance.
  • Experience propagating rare, endangered, difficult-to-propagate, or high-value plant species is highly desirable.
  • Strong practical experience in explant selection, preparation, surface sterilisation, and aseptic handling.
  • Demonstrated experience preparing and modifying plant tissue culture media and working with plant growth regulators.
  • Extensive experience maintaining sterile laboratory conditions and controlling contamination.
  • Hands-on experience operating autoclaves, laminar-flow cabinets, growth chambers, pH meters, balances, microscopes, and related laboratory equipment.
  • Experience identifying and troubleshooting contamination, culture decline, abnormal growth, poor multiplication, and rooting problems.
  • Experience monitoring environmental conditions for in-vitro cultures.
  • Experience with hardening and acclimatisation of tissue-cultured plants to greenhouse or nursery environments.
  • Experience developing, testing, refining, or documenting species-specific micropropagation protocols.
  • Strong laboratory record-keeping, data-management, inventory-management, and technical documentation skills.
  • Experience supporting plant conservation, ex-situ conservation, or endangered species propagation projects is preferred.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with botanists, horticulturists, researchers, conservation specialists, and academic institutions.
  • Demonstrated ability to train staff, interns, students, or laboratory personnel in tissue culture techniques.
  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, observational, and problem-solving skills.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to perform laboratory procedures consistently and precisely.
  • Previous experience in a botanic garden, plant tissue culture laboratory, research institution, university, conservation facility, commercial micropropagation laboratory, or comparable plant-science environment is preferred

title: NPI Formulatie Operator (Tijdelijk Assignment 1,5j)
description:
NPI Operator Filling

Afdeling

De Small Scale Fill Finish (S2F2) afdeling maakt deel uit van de Clinical Supply afdeling en maakt de lancering van nieuwe, innovatieve geneesmiddelen en vaccins mogelijk door het ontwikkelen en implementeren van nieuwe productie processen, het produceren van klinische stalen en het verwerven van product en proces kennis.

Het volledige productie proces wordt van A tot Z verzorgd door het team van de pilot plant: reinigen en steriliseren van equipment en cleanrooms, afwegen en dooien van grondstoffen, formulatie van oplossingen en suspensies, steriele filtratie, steriel afvullen van vials/spuiten en het vriesdrogen van het afgevulde product, …

In de pilot plant wordt gebruik gemaakt van divers farmaceutische equipment en processen en wordt gewerkt volgens dezelfde kwaliteitsstandaarden als in een commerciële farmaceutische productie plant.

Verantwoordelijkheden en opportuniteiten

Binnen clinical supply/S2F2 zijn we op zoek naar een tijdelijke versterking voor ons team gedurende 1,5 jaar. Een ideale opportuniteit om te ontdekken of de clinical supply/S2F2 wereld iets voor jou is.

Als New Product Introduction (NPI) filling operator werk je mee aan de ontwikkeling van nieuwe geneesmiddelen en vaccins. Deze diverse producten vereisen elk een specifiek afvulproces en specifiek afvulequipment, waardoor je de kans krijgt om met een brede waaier van processen en equipment te werken.

Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het afvullen van oplossingen, suspensies en RNA-suspensies:

· Je zorgt voor de omstelling, set-up, bediening, monitoring en bijsturing de spuitenlijn in grade C (debagger) en in grade A/B (deliner, filling unit, stoppering unit).

· Je voert de omstelling, set-up, bediening, monitoring en bijsturing van de vial lijn uit in grade C (washer, tunnel, capper, trayer) en grade A/B (filler, stoppering unit, alus).

· Je bedient de vriesdroger en zorgt ook voor uitvoering van de CIP, SIP, WIT van de vriesdroger.

· Je voert integriteitstesten uit van de filters en van RABS handschoenen.

· Je leert in de toekomst werken met een modulaire isolator lijn (Variosys)

· Je neemt in-proces stalen zoals vereist voor de vrijgave maar ook voor de ontwikkeling van het nieuwe geneesmiddel of vaccin.

· Je assembleert productspecifieke vulpaden en zorgt voor de sterilisatie van dit equipment volgens gevalideerde procedures.

· Je reinigt het filling equipment en volgt hierbij strikt de quarantaine regels die verbonden zijn aan de lopende cleaning validatie voor het nieuwe geneesmiddelen of vaccin. Je reinigt ook de afvullijn en de cleanrooms.

· Je zorgt voor het periodieke onderhoud van het S2F2 filling equipment en lokalen.

· Je assisteert bij preventief onderhoud van het filling equipment.

· Je assisteert bij andere teams (formulatie of andere afdeling) indien nodig

· …

Functieprofiel

Must

  • Je werkt accuraat
  • Kwaliteit, orde en netheid zijn op je buik geschreven
  • Je volgt strikt procedures en documenteert nauwkeurig
  • Je werkt vlot in team
  • Goed proces en technisch inzicht
  • Je kan zelfstandig werken
  • Je communiceert goed en respectvol naar TL, shift PE, teamleden van zelfde en andere shift
  • Je kan goed tegen wisselende prioriteiten en planningswijzigingen (eigen aan clinical supply)

Nice to have

  • Ervaring in een vergelijkbare functie
  • Ervaring in een GMP omgeving
  • Ervaring in een aseptische werkomgeving

Work Location Assignment: On Premise

De Pfizer site in Puurs is één van de grootste productie- en verpakkingssites van Pfizer wereldwijd, gespecialiseerd in aseptische productie en verpakking. Jaarlijks worden in Puurs meer dan 400 miljoen doses injecteerbare vaccins en medicijnen geproduceerd. Deze zijn ter plaatse verpakt in ampullen, flacons, plastic flessen, spuiten en patronen voor pennen.

De medicijnen die in Puurs worden gemaakt, zijn bestemd voor patiënten in meer dan 170 landen wereldwijd. 30% van de productie uit Puurs is bestemd voor ontwikkelingslanden, in samenwerking met UNICEF, WHO, GAVI en ngo's.

Met het gebruik van twee windturbines, zonnepanelen en een warmtekrachtcentrale richten we ons op hernieuwbare energie.

Pfizer’s doel is om gelijke kansen te bieden in het wervingsproces door elke vorm van vooringenomenheid of mogelijke discriminatie te vermijden, ongeacht (maar niet beperkt tot) geslacht, leeftijd, ras, religie of overtuiging, seksuele geaardheid of handicap. We creëren een organisatie en bevorderen een cultuur die respect heeft voor ieders unieke karakter en levenservaringen en die de diversiteit van onze samenleving, klanten en markten weerspiegelt. Dit bereiken we door een omgeving te cultiveren en in stand te houden waarin elke collega zich gewaardeerd en ondersteund voelt.

Disability Inclusion:

Onze missie is om de kracht van al onze mensen te ontwikkelen en ruimte te geven. We zijn trots om een inclusieve werkgever te zijn, die aan alle kandidaten met een beperking gelijke kansen biedt. We moedigen je aan om jezelf te zijn en dat met ons te delen, wetende dat wij ons best gaan doen om jouw sollicitatie en toekomstige carrière te ondersteunen. Jouw reis bij Pfizer begint hier!

title: Databricks Forward Deployed Engineer (AI/ML)
description:
Engagement Type: Independent Contractor (1099)

Primary Point of Contact: Product Manager and Practice Leader

Location: Remote (LATAM Based)

At RevStar, we build cutting-edge cloud, data, and Generative AI solutions that transform how enterprise organizations operate. As a strategic partner in the AWS and Databricks ecosystems, we don’t just deliver code—we solve complex business problems, modernize legacy data estates, and deploy production-grade AI applications that drive real business value.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Senior Databricks Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to join our growing Data & AI Practice. In this highly visible role, you will work embedded directly at the intersection of technical architecture, hands-on engineering, and executive client engagement.

As an FDE, you are both a master builder and a trusted technical advisor. You will own the full delivery lifecycle for high-impact enterprise accounts—designing scalable data foundations, implementing cutting-edge Generative AI solutions, and migrating complex workloads onto the Databricks Lakehouse platform. Simultaneously, you will drive customer adoption and consumption growth by identifying new use cases and building strategic alignment with client technical leadership.

Key Responsibilities

  • Hands-on Solution Architecture & Engineering: Design, build, and deploy production-grade data pipelines, analytics engines, and Generative AI/LLM applications using the Databricks platform, Spark, Python/PySpark, and modern cloud ecosystems (AWS/Azure/GCP).
  • Enterprise Customer Delivery: Serve as the primary technical leader on strategic enterprise client engagements. Partner with C-level executives, VP/Directors of Data, and engineering teams to translate business challenges into high-performing technical solutions.
  • Databricks Migration & Estate Modernization: Lead complex legacy platform migrations (e.g., Snowflake, Teradata, legacy Hadoop, SQL Server) onto the Databricks Lakehouse architecture.
  • GenAI & Advanced Analytics Implementation: Guide enterprise customers (Healthcare, Retail, Financial Services, etc.) in adopting GenAI solutions, RAG architectures, model fine-tuning, and MLflow/Databricks Mosaic AI integrations.
  • Drive Platform Adoption & Growth: Partner with account leadership to identify new, high-value technical use cases across client business units, expanding Databricks platform usage and driving measurable ROI for clients.
  • Technical Mentorship & Practice Building: Mentor and coach junior Solution Engineers, Architects, and Consultants. Contribute to internal RevStar code libraries, reusable accelerators, and technical delivery best practices.

Requirements

Technical Expertise:

  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in Data Engineering, Machine Learning, or Solutions Architecture.
  • 3+ years of deep technical experience within the Databricks Ecosystem (Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, MLflow, Spark/PySpark, Databricks Workflows/Jobs, Mosaic AI).
  • Generative AI / ML: Practical experience designing and deploying RAG pipelines, fine-tuning LLMs, working with vector databases, and managing ML pipelines end-to-end.
  • Cloud Architecture: Strong expertise in cloud-native architectures (AWS preferred—S3, Glue, Lambda, Redshift, etc.).
  • Data Migration: Proven track record of migrating enterprise legacy data warehouses/lakes onto Databricks.
  • Databricks Certifications: Databricks Certified Data Engineer Professional and/or Machine Learning Professional preferred.

Client & Business Acumen:

  • Enterprise Experience: Demonstrated track record of leading technical delivery for Fortune 500 or large enterprise clients (Healthcare, Retail, Consumer Goods experience is a strong plus).
  • Consulting & Customer-Facing Skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication skills; comfortable presenting technical architecture, building POCs/demos, and managing client stakeholders up to the C-suite.
  • Growth Mindset: Ability to spot technical expansion opportunities within existing client accounts and serve as a technical advocate to grow account footprint.

Benefits

Engagement Details & Terms

    • Contract Status: Independent Contractor (Form 1099-NEC).
    • Compensation: Hourly rate, commensurate with experience.

title: Vil du bli en del av teamet hos MENY Nesttun Senter? Vi søker serviceinnstilte og allsidige MATarbeidere til kasse, kolonial og Post i Butikk
description:
I MENY elsker vi mat! For oss er god mat en lidenskap, og noe av det viktigste som finnes. Hos oss er alle MATarbeidere, uansett om du jobber i ferskvaredisken, kolonialen, i kassen eller på kontoret. Å være en MATarbeider i MENY betyr at du alltid gjør ditt beste for å veilede og inspirere kundene våre til matglede. Sammen skal vi hjelpe flere å spise bedre, og leve bedre.


Stillingsomfang: 30-60%
Arbeidstid: dag, kveld og helg
Oppstart: 01.08.2026 - eller etter avtale

Søknadsfrist: søknader behandles fortløpende


For å søke må du være fylt 18 år og du må også kunne kommunisere godt med kunder og kollegaer på norsk.


Hvem er du, og hva skal du gjøre?

Som MATarbeider i MENY vil du ha en variert og aktiv arbeidshverdag. Dine arbeidsoppgaver vil i stor grad bestå i varepåfylling, rullering og fremtrekk. Du vil også ekspedere i kassa, tømme panteautomaten, hente kundevogner og hjelpe kunder. I kolonialavdelingen vil du arbeide med tørrvarer, frossenvarer, meieriprodukter samt øl og mineralvann, som sammen utgjør en betydelig del av butikkens sortiment. I tillegg kan det være perioder der du blir tildelt oppgaver i andre avdelinger.


Post i butikk

Hos oss finner du også Post i Butikk, hvor arbeidsoppgavene i hovedsak vil bestå av registrering av innkommende pakker og brevforsendelser ved leveranser fra Posten. Du vil også bistå i utlevering og mottak av sendinger i henhold til gjeldende rutiner og krav fra Posten og MENY. Stillingen innebærer også betjening av Postens CashGuard-system, kontanthåndtering, salg av frimerker og andre postrelaterte produkter, samt øvrige oppgaver som naturlig hører til avdelingen. Du vil få grundig opplæring og nødvendig støtte for å lykkes i rollen.


Fordi du skal hjelpe kunder og samarbeide tett med kollegaer, ser vi etter deg som liker å snakke med mennesker og brenner for god kundeservice. Om du er student, har hull i cv’en eller ikke har arbeidserfaring, er vi ikke så opptatt av. Det viktigste er at du er lærevillig, blid og liker å stå på. Du må kunne løfte tungt og takle å gå mange skritt, for her skjer det alltid noe! En deltidsstilling hos oss kan åpne veien for større ansvar og nye utfordringer for dem som viser initiativ og engasjement.


Hvordan er det å jobbe i MENY?
Hos oss vil du blant annet lære å ta ansvar, mestre stress, håndtere mennesker og ikke minst butikkdrift. Vi har en interaktiv kursplattform, ulike klasseromskurs som gir deg faglig påfyll og et traineeprogram med fokus på å gå fra ansatt til å bli leder, for å nevne noe. Satser du på MENY, satser MENY på deg!


Når det gjelder trivsel på jobb, vil vi trekke frem samholdet. title: ELA Interventionist (Nellis) 89156
description:
We're excited to provide the best education in the best environment to our students!


Academies of Math and Science – Nellis Campus
ELA Interventionist
Location: 1780 Betty Ln, Las Vegas, NV 89156
Start Date: 2026–2027 School Year
Compensation Range: $54,000 – $60,813 annually (DOE)


Position Overview

Academies of Math and Science (AMS) is a network of high-performing K–8 public charter schools committed to academic excellence, college readiness, and equitable access to high-quality education for students in historically underserved communities.

AMS is seeking a passionate, data-driven, and student-focused ELA Interventionist to provide targeted literacy support to scholars who need additional assistance developing their reading, writing, comprehension, and language skills.

The ELA Interventionist will work closely with classroom teachers, instructional leaders, and support staff to identify student needs, provide targeted intervention, monitor progress, and adjust instruction based on student data. The ideal candidate is committed to helping all scholars make meaningful academic growth while maintaining high expectations and creating a supportive, engaging learning environment.


Key Responsibilities

ELA Intervention & Student Achievement

  • Provide targeted, standards-aligned ELA intervention to students performing below grade-level expectations
  • Deliver small-group and individualized instruction focused on reading comprehension, fluency, vocabulary, phonics, writing, and language skills as appropriate
  • Use student assessment data to identify skill gaps and develop targeted intervention plans
  • Implement evidence-based instructional strategies to accelerate student literacy growth
  • Provide differentiated instruction based on individual student needs, skill levels, and learning goals
  • Reinforce grade-level ELA standards and classroom instruction through targeted intervention
  • Monitor student progress through formative assessments, progress-monitoring tools, and classroom data
  • Adjust intervention strategies and instructional plans based on student performance
  • Maintain accurate documentation of student intervention plans, progress, and outcomes
  • Support students in developing confidence, independence, and positive attitudes toward reading and writing

Data Analysis & Progress Monitoring

  • Regularly analyze assessment and progress-monitoring data to identify trends and areas of need
  • Establish measurable academic goals for students receiving intervention services
  • Track student growth and communicate progress with classroom teachers and instructional leaders
  • Participate in data meetings and intervention planning sessions
  • Use data to determine when students require additional, modified, or reduced intervention support
  • Collaborate with teachers to ensure intervention strategies are aligned with classroom instruction
  • Identify students who may benefit from additional academic or instructional supports

Classroom Culture & Student Support

  • Establish a positive, structured, and supportive learning environment
  • Build strong relationships with students while maintaining high academic expectations
  • Encourage student engagement, perseverance, and confidence in reading and writing
  • Implement PBIS and preventative intervention strategies
  • Provide an inclusive learning environment that supports students with diverse academic and linguistic needs
  • Support students’ academic, behavioral, and social-emotional development
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and academically focused intervention environment

Collaboration & Professional Growth

  • Collaborate regularly with classroom teachers, instructional leaders, special education staff, and other support personnel
  • Participate in weekly professional development and professional learning communities
  • Work with grade-level teams to coordinate intervention strategies and academic supports
  • Share student progress, instructional strategies, and data with relevant staff
  • Participate in MTSS/RTI processes and intervention planning as appropriate
  • Continue developing knowledge of evidence-based literacy practices and intervention strategies
  • Contribute to school-wide initiatives focused on literacy achievement and continuous improvement

Family Engagement

  • Communicate with families regarding student academic progress and intervention goals
  • Provide appropriate updates regarding student growth, areas of need, and strategies for continued support
  • Collaborate with families to encourage reading and academic practice at home
  • Participate in parent-teacher conferences and other family engagement opportunities as needed

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must meet the following requirements:

  • Valid teaching license issued by the Nevada Department of Education (NDE) with a K–8 endorsement
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in English, English Language Arts, Education, Reading, Literacy, or a related field
  • Demonstrated ability to provide differentiated instruction and targeted academic intervention
  • Strong understanding of reading comprehension, writing, vocabulary, and literacy development
  • Ability to analyze student data and use it to guide instructional decisions
  • Demonstrated ability to establish positive relationships with students and maintain a structured learning environment
  • Commitment to serving Title I and multilingual learner communities
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with teachers, instructional leaders, and support staff

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience as an ELA, reading, literacy, or intervention teacher
  • Experience providing small-group or individualized academic intervention
  • Experience working with students performing below grade-level expectations
  • Experience with MTSS/RTI or other multi-tiered intervention systems
  • Experience working in Title I schools
  • Experience supporting English Language Learners and multilingual students
  • Knowledge of evidence-based literacy intervention strategies
  • Experience using assessment and progress-monitoring data to drive instruction
  • Strong communication, organization, and data-analysis skills
  • Bilingual (Spanish-English) preferred

Compensation & Benefits

AMS offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support professional growth and long-term career success.

  • Competitive salary based on years of K–12 teacher-of-record experience
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contributions

Medical, dental, life, and disability insurance


Join us to enjoy rewarding challenges and ongoing opportunities!

title: IT Auditor
description:

Oversees project team members as they execute the audit and provides coaching/feedback to team members.

title: Lead Refrigeration Systems Engineer
description:
Be a part of our mission! As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies, and through our businesses including Trane® and Thermo King, sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business. Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities? Do you want to contribute to making a better future? If the answer is yes, we invite you to consider joining us in boldly challenging what's possible for a sustainable world.

Learn about our benefits designed for you to Thrive at work and at home.

We boldly go.

Where is the work:

Monday to Thursday, work onsite with your colleagues. Fridays, choose your work location, balancing what your work requires.

What's in it for you:

Trane Technologies is seeking an experienced Lead Refrigeration Systems Engineer to join our Trane Commercial Systems organization and responsible for all aspects of equipment design and component integration for Trane Commercial Water-to-Water product lines. This includes having the technical expertise to model system performance, support new technology projects, create system and subsystem DFMEA documentation, develop and lead product design, supervise product validation testing, and drive quality and reliability issues to root cause. This position interacts with other functional resource groups to support product design and integration, such as Compressor Engineering, Thermal Systems, Controls, Electrical, Manufacturing, etc. To be successful, this Lead Refrigeration Systems Engineer will need to collaborate closely with Chiller Engineering teams located in La Crosse, WI and Pueblo, CO along with support organizations located in Shanghai, China and Bangalore, India.


What you will do:

  • Design and innovate HVAC refrigeration systems with a focus on achieving performance standards, meeting sustainability targets, complying with regulatory requirements, attaining quality goals, and adhering to cost targets.
  • Lead projects, typically involving major system development consistent with the company gate review process, to plan, conduct, and coordinate engineering assignments, prepare schedules, report status to leadership, and meet project milestones.
  • Create and execute computer models to simulate and predict unit performance. Analyze system issues using appropriate modeling tools and techniques. Where needed, collaborate with modeling and simulation specialists to develop new tools.
  • Govern and lead design reviews through processes such as FMEA, DFMEA, DVP&R, and Risk Analysis.
  • Create mechanical designs for systems and subsystems that leverage chiller and heat pump architecture and meet agency, code, structural, and serviceability requirements.
  • Incorporate Design For Manufacturing (DFM) features to support efficient factory build processes.
  • Develop laboratory test plans, conduct testing, analyze test data, including use of Six Sigma tools, statistical analysis techniques, and applying Design for Reliability principles, and interpret results and execute design updates based on the results.
  • Evaluate complex, special, and advanced engineering tasks working independently as an expert with minimal supervision.
  • Serve as subject matter expert on capabilities to improve existing systems and processes. Collaborate with and influence product teams to achieve common objectives.
  • Provide intensive technical guidance and leadership to less experienced professionals or technicians and other team members.
  • Develop and document HVAC system level modes, sequence of operations, and other system level control requirements.
  • Provide key technical support in pursuit of Trane business, including participation on strategic job acquisition teams.
  • Develop and/or update Trane purchased part Engineering Specifications.
  • Support field and factory system problem resolution.
  • Define, identify, and complete appropriate qualification testing activities.
  • Guide overall component choices for system design employing industry wide best practices.
  • Guide and drive short term resiliency challenges to reduce risk in the product portfolio.
  • Effectively meet the needs of internal and external customers, through documenting, reviewing and prioritizing customer requirements.
  • Ability to travel both domestically and abroad up to two weeks at a time. Able to attain the necessary visa for travel when applicable. Expected travel time ~ 10%.

What you will bring:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering (or a directly related discipline) and at least 10+ years of engineering work experience is required. Mechanical Engineering is preferred. Master's Degree in Engineering is a plus.
  • HVAC engineering background in chilled and heating water systems.
  • Experience with product design, bill of materials, engineering specifications, and product manufacturing. Understanding of HVAC system functions including refrigeration, heat transfer, airflow, and ventilation.
  • Experience with application of various components used within HVAC systems such as coils, compressors, motors, and fans.
  • Experience launching products that meet UL, CSA, or CE agency standards.
  • Understanding of statistics as applied to product reliability.
  • Ability to apply heat transfer and fluid flow concepts for real world problem solving.
  • Ability to efficiently understand, condense, and organize information necessary to make engineering decisions along with having the ability to be coached and mentored by Senior employees.
  • Design or application experience with HVAC products, thermodynamic computations, pressure vessel design, compressor, motor, controls, or heat transfer technologies and understanding of Data & Analytics, making data driven decisions and programming knowledge is a plus.
  • Strong technical skills with a natural technical curiosity and an enthusiasm to learn and develop new skills.
  • Must have good verbal communications skills and good technical writing and documentation skills.
  • Must be a self-starter with a high energy level and a high commitment to career.
  • Must have the ability to understand, condense, and organize information necessary to make engineering decisions quickly and efficiently.
  • Technically creative yet grounded in real world feasibility.
  • Able to perform thorough and objective analysis.
  • Ability to work as an effective member of a diverse team and able to collaborate with and influence others.
  • Willing and able to transfer knowledge to other groups.
  • Exhibit a polished and professional demeanor when interacting with customers, while actively engaging with professional societies.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in coordinating supplier capabilities effectively.
  • Good stand-up skills in front of customers and the field sales force.

title: Senior AI Product Engineer (React / Typescript) - UX
description:
Landytech is on a mission to revolutionise the way that investment managers, asset owners and their advisors access asset information. Powered by Sesame, an industry-leading investment reporting platform, we are helping clients in over 15 countries make informed investment decisions and deliver insights faster.

The company is growing rapidly and it’s an exciting time to join, having secured $12M in Series B funding in January 2023. In just four years, it has gone from two co-founders to a team of 80+ staff, with offices in London and Paris. At Landytech, we see diversity as our strength with a team from over 15 countries and 14 languages spoken.

The role

AI has made producing screens easy. It has not made products coherent. We are looking for someone to own the experience of Sesame end to end — the client journey, the interaction logic, the look and feel, and the consistency of all of it — and to build it.

If you are an engineer who has always had a view on how the product should look and behave, this is a role where that judgement is part of the remit rather than a side interest.

We have posted this role under two titles — Design Engineer and Product Experience Designer — to reach both backgrounds. Same role, same team. Apply once, to whichever fits you better.

How we work

We have rebuilt our product process around AI rather than bolting it on:

• AI is used heavily at every stage of both design and engineering, not just at the production end

• Our design system lives in code, used by engineers and AI tooling alike

• Tooling changes every few months and we expect it to

You will have real scope to shape how we work, and to help build the parts that do not exist yet.

What you will shape

How much of this you lead outright will depend on your experience and on how it fits with the team already in place. There is room to take on more over time.

  • The front-end experience layer. You will build the interfaces that matter most, particularly the dense and difficult ones, and help set the patterns others follow
  • The design system. Developed in code with the rest of the front-end team, with a leading voice in what belongs in the system
  • Look, feel and consistency. The product should feel like one thing, and you will help define what that one thing is and uphold it in review and in tooling
  • The client journey. You will be in front of investment professionals, family offices and their advisors, and trusted to act on what you hear
  • Craft in dense financial interfaces. Tables legible at scale, numbers at the right precision, drill-downs that survive a messy real portfolio under load

The must-have: setting the standard AI works to

AI is very good at producing attractive interfaces. Given a design system, almost anyone can now generate a credible screen.

The harder problem, and the one this role exists to solve, is making sure what we build expresses the product’s logic, density and intent rather than simply reusing its components. That means defining the standards and instructions our tools work to, reading the output critically enough to see why something is subtly wrong, and tightening the rules so it does not recur.

Using AI to produce interfaces is not the skill we are looking for. Directing it to our standard, consistently and at depth, is.

Increasingly this is engineering work: it lives in the repo, in the tooling, and in what the agents can and cannot reach for.

Strongly valued: design expertise

We are not looking for a front-end engineer willing to tolerate design work. We are looking for real UX judgement.

  • You can say what is wrong with a flow, not just implement it faster
  • You think in objects, relationships and states before components
  • You have taste in what matters here: hierarchy, typography, density, restraint
  • You are comfortable doing the upstream thinking, including what should not exist at all

No portfolio required. Shipped interfaces we can look at, and the decisions behind them, is what we want to see.

Also valued: product management instincts

If you have talked to clients directly, decided what not to build, and owned an outcome rather than a ticket, we will weight it heavily.

What we are looking for

We do not expect anyone to have everything below — we would rather meet someone exceptional in two areas than adequate in all three.

  • 5+ years in front-end engineering, ideally React and TypeScript, with libraries such as shadcn/ui
  • Experience building and maintaining a design system in production, not just consuming one
  • Data-dense interfaces at scale — virtualised tables, charting, performance under real load
  • Fluency with AI-assisted development, and the specification skill described above
  • Willingness to work directly with users and own the experience, not the implementation alone
  • Comfortable as an editor and enabler: reviewing others’ work, teaching, holding a line
  • Genuine curiosity about finance. You need not arrive knowing what a capital call is

Our process

Our interview process is likely to include a portfolio or work conversation, a short practical exercise based on a real Sesame flow, and a working session with a product manager and an engineer. We adapt the steps to the candidate and will always tell you what to expect in advance.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and stock options
  • Hybrid working
  • Private medical insurance with Bupa for you and your family
  • Death in service insurance option
  • Pension plan with NEST
  • Cycle to Work scheme and gym allowance
  • Office food and drinks, regular socials

title: Plant Propagator (Saudi Arabia)
description:
The Plant Propagator is responsible for the propagation, establishment, and management of plant material required to support the Botanic Gardens’ living collections, displays, conservation programmes, and horticulture operations. The role applies a range of propagation methods, including seeds, cuttings, grafting, division, and other vegetative techniques, to produce healthy and genetically appropriate plant stock.

The Plant Propagator will manage nursery areas and propagation stock, develop and refine propagation protocols for rare, endangered, and difficult-to-propagate species, and monitor plants through the different stages of establishment. The role will maintain detailed propagation records and evaluate success rates to continuously improve propagation techniques and support the long-term sustainability and conservation value of the Botanic Gardens' plant collections.

The work location would be in Thuwwal, Saudi Arabia.


Scope of Work

  • Propagate plants using a range of techniques, including seeds, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering, division, and other appropriate vegetative propagation methods.
  • Select appropriate propagation techniques according to species characteristics, seasonal requirements, plant condition, and collection objectives.
  • Collect, prepare, process, and appropriately store seeds and vegetative propagation material.
  • Assess the quality and viability of propagation material prior to use.
  • Prepare appropriate propagation media and containers according to species-specific requirements.
  • Apply appropriate seed treatments, including scarification, stratification, soaking, or other pre-germination treatments where required.
  • Prepare and treat cuttings and other vegetative material to promote successful rooting and establishment.
  • Undertake grafting, budding, division, and other specialist propagation activities where appropriate.
  • Monitor germination, rooting, establishment, growth, and overall plant health throughout the propagation process.
  • Propagate plants using a range of techniques, including seeds, cuttings, grafting, budding, layering, division, and other appropriate vegetative propagation methods.
  • Select appropriate propagation techniques according to species characteristics, seasonal requirements, plant condition, and collection objectives.
  • Collect, prepare, process, and appropriately store seeds and vegetative propagation material.
  • Assess the quality and viability of propagation material prior to use.
  • Prepare appropriate propagation media and containers according to species-specific requirements.
  • Apply appropriate seed treatments, including scarification, stratification, soaking, or other pre-germination treatments where required.
  • Prepare and treat cuttings and other vegetative material to promote successful rooting and establishment.
  • Undertake grafting, budding, division, and other specialist propagation activities where appropriate.
  • Monitor germination, rooting, establishment, growth, and overall plant health throughout the propagation process.
  • Identify and address propagation problems, including poor germination, rooting failure, disease, pest infestation, nutrient deficiencies, and environmental stress.
  • Manage and maintain nursery and propagation areas, ensuring appropriate growing conditions, hygiene, organisation, and plant-care standards.
  • Manage nursery plant stock to meet the requirements of garden collections, seasonal displays, replacement planting, conservation programmes, and other horticulture activities.
  • Monitor and manage irrigation, humidity, shade, temperature, growing media, fertilisation, and plant nutrition within propagation and nursery areas.
  • Coordinate the movement of successfully propagated plants from propagation areas into nursery, greenhouse, indoor, or outdoor garden environments.
  • Support appropriate hardening and acclimatisation of young plants prior to establishment within garden collections.
  • Develop, test, document, and refine species-specific propagation protocols, particularly for rare, endangered, sensitive, and difficult-to-propagate plant species.
  • Conduct propagation trials to identify methods that improve germination, rooting, survival, and establishment rates.
  • Collaborate with curators, botanists, horticulturists, conservation specialists, and other technical staff to identify propagation priorities.
  • Support ex situ conservation and collection-development programmes through propagation of priority plant species.
  • Ensure propagation activities maintain appropriate provenance and collection information for conservation and scientifically important material.
  • Maintain detailed records of propagation activities, methods, source material, dates, treatments, environmental conditions, quantities, germination rates, rooting rates, losses, and overall success rates.
  • Maintain accurate nursery stock inventories and update relevant plant collection or propagation databases.
  • Analyse propagation outcomes and use results to improve future propagation protocols and practices.
  • Implement appropriate nursery hygiene, sanitation, plant-health, and biosecurity procedures.
  • Support Integrated Pest Management (IPM) within nursery and propagation areas.
  • Maintain propagation tools, equipment, facilities, and work areas in a clean, safe, and operational condition.
  • Ensure propagation activities comply with applicable health and safety, environment, biosecurity, and horticulture operating procedures.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Horticulture, Botany, Plant Sciences, Plant Biology, or a related discipline.
  • Specialist training or certification in plant propagation, nursery management, seed technology, grafting, or related horticulture disciplines is advantageous.
  • Additional training in rare plant propagation, seed conservation, nursery biosecurity, or plant conservation is advantageous.
  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant professional experience in plant propagation and nursery horticulture.
  • Demonstrated experience propagating plants using multiple methods, including seeds and cuttings.
  • Practical experience with grafting, budding, layering, division, and other vegetative propagation techniques is highly desirable.
  • Experience selecting, collecting, preparing, and handling seed and vegetative propagation material.
  • Demonstrated experience with seed germination, dormancy-breaking treatments, and seedling establishment.
  • Practical experience preparing and rooting cuttings using appropriate growing media, environmental conditions, and rooting treatments.
  • Experience managing nursery areas and plant stock for botanic, horticulture, landscape, conservation, or comparable plant collections.
  • Experience monitoring and managing irrigation, humidity, temperature, shade, growing media, and plant nutrition within nursery and propagation environments.
  • Experience monitoring plant health and addressing pests, diseases, nutrient deficiencies, and environmental stresses during propagation.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, testing, or refining plant propagation protocols.
  • Experience propagating rare, endangered, sensitive, or difficult-to-propagate species is preferred.
  • Experience supporting ex situ conservation, botanical collection development, or conservation propagation programmes is advantageous.
  • Experience with the hardening, acclimatisation, and establishment of propagated plants into nursery, greenhouse, or garden environments.
  • Demonstrated experience maintaining detailed propagation records and monitoring germination, rooting, survival, and success rates.
  • Experience maintaining nursery stock inventories and plant provenance or accession information.
  • Experience implementing nursery hygiene, sanitation, biosecurity, and Integrated Pest Management practices.
  • Experience collaborating with horticulturists, botanists, curators, researchers, and conservation specialists on propagation programmes.
  • Previous experience within a botanic garden, nursery, arboretum, conservation facility, research institution, seed facility, or comparable horticulture environment is preferred.

I KIWI er det kunden som er sjefen, og for å gjøre sjefen fornøyd trenger vi Norges blideste og hyggeligste medarbeidere. Er det deg? Har du også en god porsjon konkurranseinstinkt og «stå-på-vilje»? Da må du lese videre.

Gjennom årene har KIWI vært den soleklare vekstvinneren i det norske dagligvaremarkedet. Hver eneste medarbeider er viktig i KIWI og gjennom å gjøre hverandre bedre skal vi vinne kundene. Nå søker vi deg som vil være med på det grønne vinnerlaget, og bidra til å ta oss videre.

Som butikkmedarbeider med låseansvar vil du ha arbeidsoppgaver som varepåfylling og betjening av kunder. I tillegg vil du ha utvidet ansvar når butikksjef, assisterende butikksjef eller andre med låseansvar ikke er jobb.

Vi søker en fremoverlent og positiv person som kan bidra til at butikken fortsetter å levere gode handleopplevelser for kunden. Er du klar for å bli med på det grønne vinnerlaget, og bidra til å ta oss videre?

Vi leter etter deg som:

  • Har fylt 18 år
  • Har erfaring fra dagligvarebransje, men ingen betingelse
  • Er tydelig, strukturert og positiv i møte med kolleger og kunder
  • Har stor arbeidskapasitet og trives med en hektisk hverdag
  • Er ærlig, ansvarsbevisst og til å stole på

Vi kan tilby:

  • En sosial og trivelig arbeidsplass med masse hyggelige kolleger
  • Grundig opplæring
  • Konkurransedyktig betingelser
  • Spennende utviklingsmuligheter

Med over 700 butikker og 54 milliarder i omsetning, er KIWI Minipris landets største lavpriskjede. KIWI Minipris er en del av NorgesGruppen, som er landets største dagligvaregruppering. I KIWI mener vi at mangfold beriker, og våre medarbeidere skal speile befolkningen. Vi oppfordrer alle kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke, uavhengig av kjønn, alder, nasjonalitet eller etnisk bakgrunn.

title: Fire Life Safety Director
description:

Our highly trained professionals specialize in hospitality, events, and investigative security. We pride ourselves on delivering tailored security solutions with professionalism, reliability, and expertise.

title: Regional Director, Dermatology Access & Reimbursement – Northeast
description:
Band

Level 6


Job Description Summary

#LI-Remote

This is a field-based and remote opportunity supporting a team in an assigned geography.
Novartis is unable to offer relocation support for this role. Please only apply if this location is accessible to you.

Company will not sponsor visas for this position.

The Regional Director, Access & Reimbursement is a strategic field leadership role responsible for guiding and developing a customer-focused team dedicated to helping patients navigate access to Novartis therapies. This leader partners closely with cross-functional colleagues to ensure customers receive exceptional, compliant support throughout the patient’s access journey. The role combines people leadership, operational excellence, business strategy, and regional oversight to drive meaningful impact for patients, customers, and the organization. Success in this position requires collaboration, thoughtful decision-making, and a commitment to fostering an inclusive, forward-thinking culture that empowers teams to thrive. As a visible leader and trusted partner, the Regional Director helps translate strategy into action while advancing enterprise goals with integrity, accountability, and excellence.


Job Description

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead, inspire, and develop a customer-focused team of Access & Reimbursement professionals, fostering a culture of growth, accountability, and excellence.
  • Attract, recruit, onboard, and retain top talent while supporting ongoing learning and career development.
  • Build and strengthen an inclusive team environment that reflects Novartis Values & Behaviors and encourages innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Translate national strategies into impactful regional execution that advances business objectives and enhances customer and patient experience.
  • Coach teams to proactively identify and address patient access and reimbursement challenges, helping remove barriers to therapy initiation and continuation.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional colleagues across field and headquarters organizations to ensure aligned, customer-focused, and compliant execution.
  • Anticipate, escalate, and help resolve access-related issues by collaborating effectively within a matrixed environment.
  • Serve as a trusted regional leader, building strong partnerships that support operational excellence and meaningful outcomes for patients and customers.
  • Maintain a deep understanding of company policies, industry regulations, and compliance requirements, ensuring all activities are conducted with integrity and professionalism.
  • Contribute to regional and enterprise-wide initiatives that support organizational priorities, business performance, and long-term success.

Essential Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree required from 4-year college or university.
  • 8+ years’ experience in reimbursement, market access, contract strategy, managed care, sales, marketing, or a related healthcare field role.
  • Demonstrated leadership experience, including leading, coaching, and developing teams while collaborating across diverse stakeholders and functions.
  • Experience partnering with complex healthcare organizations, integrated delivery networks, and health systems to establish and optimize patient access pathways.
  • Strong strategic account management skills, with the ability to proactively identify and address access and reimbursement challenges impacting customers and patients.
  • Deep understanding of manufacturer-sponsored patient support programs, including specialty pharmacy distribution, buy-and-bill processes, reimbursement, billing and coding, and claims management.
  • Proven success driving business initiatives, leading through change, and executing strategic plans that deliver meaningful outcomes for patients, customers, and the organization.
  • Candidate must reside within region, or within a reasonable commuting distance to and from a metropolitan airport. Ability to travel 60-80% over a broad geography is required, with the ability to drive and/or fly within the territory. Must have a valid driver’s license.

Desirable Requirements:

  • Experience supporting specialty therapeutic areas and navigating complex practice environments, with a strong understanding of reimbursement landscapes, patient access challenges, and customer support needs.
  • Demonstrated strengths in patient support services, market access, cross-functional collaboration, launch readiness and execution, along with exceptional communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills.

Driving is an Essential Function of this Role: Meaning it is fundamental to the purpose of this job and cannot be eliminated. The company provides reasonable accommodations for otherwise qualified individuals with medical restrictions if an accommodation can be provided without eliminating the essential function of driving.

Please send accommodation requests to Eh.occupationalhealth@novartis.com.

title: Customer Repair Administrator
description:
We are a fast-paced business with ambitious growth plans; so if you are dedicated, enthusiastic and always seeking ways to improve, you'll enjoy a career with us!

Ontic is a leading global aerospace OEM trusted by the world’s aviation leaders. Ontic’s Chatsworth, CA, site specializes in precision engineering, MRO, and new solutions for parts at risk of obsolescence. With over 1,400 employees across four time zones and seven sites, we have more than doubled in size since 2019 and are continuing to grow at pace.

Our team is looking for a Customer Repair Administrator to join them. The Customer Repair Administrator will serve as the central point of coordination between Customer Service, Sales, Quality, Operations, Finance, and the customer, ensuring each return is properly tracked from initial request through receipt, evaluation, disposition, repair/replacement, shipment, and final closure.

  • Improve visibility and reporting of open returns, warranty claims, and customer issues.
  • Ensure timely communication and status updates to customers.
  • Coordinate closely with Quality and Operations to drive evaluations and dispositions.
  • Ensure credits, replacements, repairs, and associated transactions are completed and closed appropriately.
  • Free up Customer Service and Sales resources to focus on their core responsibilities and customer growth.
  • Create a standardized and controlled RMA process, improve turnaround time and customer experience, reduce open and aging returns, and establish a single point of accountability for RMAs across the business.

To be considered for the Customer Repair Administrator opening, here’s what you’ll need to bring with you:

  • High school diploma or equivalent; college degree is preferred.
  • 3-5 years of relevant experience preferably in aerospace or manufacturing environment.
  • Strong analysis and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite.

title: Math Interventionist (Nellis) 89156
description:
We're excited to provide the best education in the best environment to our students!


Academies of Math and Science – Nellis Campus
Math Interventionist
Location: 1780 Betty Ln, Las Vegas, NV 89156
Start Date: 2026–2027 School Year
Compensation Range: $54,000 – $60,813 annually (DOE)


Position Overview

Academies of Math and Science (AMS) is a network of high-performing K–8 public charter schools committed to academic excellence, college readiness, and equitable access to high-quality education for students in historically underserved communities.

AMS is seeking a passionate, data-driven, and student-focused Math Interventionist to provide targeted mathematics support to scholars who need additional assistance developing their mathematical skills, conceptual understanding, problem-solving abilities, and confidence.

The Math Interventionist will work closely with classroom teachers, instructional leaders, and support staff to identify student needs, provide targeted intervention, monitor progress, and adjust instruction based on student data. The ideal candidate is committed to helping all scholars make meaningful academic growth while maintaining high expectations and creating a supportive, engaging, and academically rigorous learning environment.

Key Responsibilities


Math Intervention & Student Achievement

  • Provide targeted, standards-aligned mathematics intervention to students performing below grade-level expectations
  • Deliver small-group and individualized instruction focused on foundational math skills, computation, fluency, number sense, problem-solving, and mathematical reasoning
  • Use student assessment data to identify skill gaps and develop targeted intervention plans
  • Implement evidence-based instructional strategies to accelerate student mathematical growth
  • Provide differentiated instruction based on individual student needs, skill levels, and learning goals
  • Reinforce grade-level math standards and classroom instruction through targeted intervention
  • Develop students’ ability to apply mathematical concepts to real-world situations and multi-step problems
  • Monitor student progress through formative assessments, progress-monitoring tools, and classroom data
  • Adjust intervention strategies and instructional plans based on student performance
  • Maintain accurate documentation of student intervention plans, progress, and outcomes
  • Support students in developing confidence, perseverance, and positive attitudes toward mathematics

Data Analysis & Progress Monitoring

  • Regularly analyze assessment and progress-monitoring data to identify trends and areas of need
  • Establish measurable academic goals for students receiving intervention services
  • Track student growth and communicate progress with classroom teachers and instructional leaders
  • Participate in data meetings and intervention planning sessions
  • Use data to determine when students require additional, modified, or reduced intervention support
  • Collaborate with teachers to ensure intervention strategies are aligned with classroom instruction
  • Identify students who may benefit from additional academic or instructional supports
  • Use student performance data to evaluate the effectiveness of intervention strategies

Classroom Culture & Student Support

  • Establish a positive, structured, and supportive learning environment
  • Build strong relationships with students while maintaining high academic expectations
  • Encourage student engagement, perseverance, and confidence in mathematics
  • Implement PBIS and preventative intervention strategies
  • Provide an inclusive learning environment that supports students with diverse academic and linguistic needs
  • Support students’ academic, behavioral, and social-emotional development
  • Maintain a safe, organized, and academically focused intervention environment

Collaboration & Professional Growth

  • Collaborate regularly with classroom teachers, instructional leaders, special education staff, and other support personnel
  • Participate in weekly professional development and professional learning communities
  • Work with grade-level teams to coordinate intervention strategies and academic supports
  • Share student progress, instructional strategies, and data with relevant staff
  • Participate in MTSS/RTI processes and intervention planning as appropriate
  • Continue developing knowledge of evidence-based mathematics intervention practices
  • Contribute to school-wide initiatives focused on mathematics achievement and continuous improvement

Family Engagement

  • Communicate with families regarding student academic progress and intervention goals
  • Provide appropriate updates regarding student growth, areas of need, and strategies for continued support
  • Collaborate with families to encourage mathematical practice and academic development at home
  • Participate in parent-teacher conferences and other family engagement opportunities as needed

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must meet the following requirements:

  • Valid teaching license issued by the Nevada Department of Education (NDE) with a K–8 endorsement
  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Mathematics, Education, Elementary Education, Secondary Education, or a related field
  • Demonstrated ability to provide differentiated instruction and targeted academic intervention
  • Strong understanding of mathematical concepts, problem-solving, number sense, and grade-level mathematics standards
  • Ability to analyze student data and use it to guide instructional decisions
  • Demonstrated ability to establish positive relationships with students and maintain a structured learning environment
  • Commitment to serving Title I and multilingual learner communities
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with teachers, instructional leaders, and support staff

Preferred Qualifications

  • Previous experience as a math, mathematics, or intervention teacher
  • Experience providing small-group or individualized academic intervention
  • Experience working with students performing below grade-level expectations
  • Experience with MTSS/RTI or other multi-tiered intervention systems
  • Experience working in Title I schools
  • Experience supporting English Language Learners and multilingual students
  • Knowledge of evidence-based mathematics intervention strategies
  • Experience using assessment and progress-monitoring data to drive instruction
  • Strong communication, organization, and data-analysis skills
  • Bilingual (Spanish-English) preferred

Compensation & Benefits

AMS offers a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support professional growth and long-term career success.

  • Competitive salary based on years of K–12 teacher-of-record experience
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contributions
  • Medical, dental, life, and disability insurance
  • Optional vision coverage
  • Performance bonuses and stipend opportunities
  • Professional development and instructional coaching
  • Opportunities for leadership growth within a growing multi-state network

title: Senior UI Artist | New Games
description:
Craft:

Job Description:

We are looking for a Senior UI Artist to help shape and produce the visual interface for our a new IP centred mobile game

This role sits between Art Direction, Game Design, UX, and Tech. Your goal is to create clear, polished, playful, and production-ready UI assets that support the game experience and match the project’s cute, quirky, and high-quality visual tone.

The ideal candidate has strong graphic design foundations, excellent iconography and illustration skills, and a good understanding of how UI is implemented in Unity. Knowledge of 3D workflows is important, and Blender experience is a plus.

Your role within the Kingdom

  • Design and produce high-quality UI assets for mobile gameplay, menus, HUDs, events, and live features.

  • Create clear, readable, and polished icons, buttons, panels, badges, frames, and interface elements.

  • Develop illustrative UI elements that support the game’s visual identity.

  • Work from wireframes, UX flows, and art direction to create final UI visuals.

  • Maintain consistency across UI screens, systems, and feature updates.

  • Prepare assets for Unity implementation with correct formats, naming, slicing, and optimization.

  • Support the creation of UI style guides, templates, and documentation.

  • Collaborate with UX, Design, Tech, and Art Direction to ensure UI is beautiful, functional, and production-ready.

  • Review in-game implementation and help polish final results.

  • Contribute ideas to improve readability, usability, and visual quality.

Collaboration and Integration

  • Work closely with Art Direction to maintain the project’s visual style.

  • Collaborate with Game Designers and UX Designers to support clear player flows.

  • Work with Unity developers to ensure UI assets integrate correctly.

  • Coordinate with 2D, 3D, VFX, and animation teams when UI requires cross-discipline support.

  • Communicate clearly with internal teams and respond well to feedback.

  • Support production priorities while keeping a strong eye on quality and consistency.

Skills to create thrills

  • Strong portfolio showing high-quality UI art for games or mobile products.

  • Excellent iconography skills with strong readability at small sizes.

  • Strong illustration skills, especially for stylized, playful, or polished game visuals.

  • Solid understanding of layout, composition, typography, color, hierarchy, and visual clarity.

  • Experience with Figma, Photoshop, Illustrator, or equivalent tools.

  • Experience creating UI assets for Unity.

  • Good knowledge of 3D principles and how 3D assets can support UI presentation.

  • Ability to prepare clean, optimized, implementation-ready assets.

  • Good understanding of mobile UI constraints and readability.

  • Experience working with art direction and established visual styles.

  • Strong communication skills and ability to take feedback constructively.

  • Good sense of polish, consistency, and quality control.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working on casual, mobile, or family-friendly games.

  • Experience with Blender.

  • Experience creating UI mockups, style guides, and asset libraries.

  • Knowledge of UI animation or motion design.

  • Comfort working with both 2D and 3D pipelines.

  • Experience supporting live game features, events, or seasonal content.

What We Offer

  • The opportunity to help shape the UI visual quality of a major global IP on mobile.

  • A collaborative art team focused on craft, clarity, and polish.

  • The chance to contribute to a playful and highly visible game experience.

  • A healthy work culture that values trust, ownership, and teamwork.

Success in this role means UI assets are clear, beautiful, consistent with the art direction, and smoothly integrated into the game.


About King

With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.

  • Documentation — Complete shift notes, incident reports, and other required documentation accurately and promptly.

  • Family Support — Provide support and information to visiting parents as directed by the treatment team.

  • Collaboration — Participate in treatment team meetings, rounds, shift reports, and patient‑specific discussions.

  • Care Planning — Review and contribute to milieu care plans; communicate updates to the interdisciplinary team.

  • Group & Activity Support — Co‑lead community meetings, social skills groups, recreation activities, and program‑specific groups.

  • Behavioral Programs — Follow individualized behavioral plans and set consistent, supportive therapeutic limits.

  • Recreation & Skill‑Building — Organize and participate in physical, social, and developmental activities for children.

title: Global Financial Crimes Negative News Vice President
description:
We're seeking someone to join our team as a Global Financial Crimes: Negative News / PEP Screening Lead in Global Financial Crimes to Lead the strategy, governance, and optimization of KYC risk-ranking and screening controls, leveraging advanced analytics and technology to enhance financial crime detection, regulatory compliance, and operational effectiveness across the Firm.

In the Legal & Compliance division, we assist the Firm in achieving its business objectives by facilitating and overseeing the Firm's management of legal, regulatory and franchise risk. This is a VP level position within the Global Financial Crimes: Know Your Customer (KYC) team which is responsible for the governance and oversight of the Firm's KYC program, including KYC policy and standards, Enterprise Customer Risk Ranking (ECRR), Negative News and PEP screening, data governance, enhanced due diligence, regulatory engagement, and monitoring of first-line execution. The function ensures that KYC controls remain effective, risk-based, compliant with regulatory requirements, and supported by robust governance and reporting.


Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.


What you'll do in the role:

- Lead the strategic enhancement and governance of KYC controls, including ECRR, Negative News Screening (NNS), and PEP screening programs.
- Drive screening model tuning, calibration, and optimization to improve risk detection, coverage, and operational efficiency.
- Leverage AI, machine learning, and advanced analytics to strengthen screening effectiveness, alert prioritization, and workflow automation.
- Partner across Compliance, Technology, Data Science, Operations, and Model Risk Management to implement and govern control enhancements.
- Analyze complex datasets to identify emerging risks, performance trends, data quality issues, and opportunities for control improvements.
- Establish and monitor key performance indicators, model effectiveness metrics, and governance standards to ensure regulatory readiness and defensibility.
- Lead assessments related to regulatory changes, new products, acquisitions, and evolving financial crime risks, translating impacts into sustainable control enhancements.
- Support audits, regulatory examinations, and senior management reporting by providing clear analytics, model rationale, and strategic recommendations.

What you'll bring to the role:

- 7+ years of experience in AML, KYC, financial crime compliance, screening analytics, model governance, or risk management within financial services or consulting.
- Demonstrated expertise in screening model tuning, calibration, optimization, and governance across adverse media, PEP, sanctions, and customer risk-rating programs.
- Proven ability to lead complex cross-functional initiatives spanning Compliance, Technology, Data, Operations, and Business stakeholders.
- Strong knowledge of financial crime screening platforms, data providers, and emerging technologies, including AI, machine learning, NLP, and advanced analytics.
- Advanced analytical and technical skills, including proficiency in SQL, Python, data analysis, and model performance measurement across large datasets.
- Deep understanding of AML, KYC, sanctions, adverse media, and PEP screening requirements, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices.
- Experience supporting model risk management, regulatory examinations, audits, technology implementations, and Agile delivery frameworks.
- Exceptional communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to influence senior stakeholders and translate complex analyses into actionable business outcomes.

Please note that the location listed for this role is temporary. The position’s work location will transition to 1445 Ross Ave, Dallas, TX 75202 at a future date. In-Person interviews will be required for the role.

title: Claims Processing Associate
company: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Michigan
description:
SUMMARY:

This role will focus on maintenance of our incoming workload, issue resolution and first report of injury (FROI) issues. This position determines jurisdiction for entry of first notice of injury (FNOI) from multiple sources and distributes to the proper destination. Enters and supports priority and special requests, including correcting newly-created claims.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

· Identifies jurisdiction, date of injury and special/additional handling items; researches and re-indexes non-new claim submissions to route to appropriate handling.

· Receives incoming general new claims calls for all entities; backup for ACD calls in the event of telephone system shutdown.

· Makes changes, corrections and updates on newly created and/or existing claims or submissions as well as guiding end-users on process techniques in various applications.

· May serve as a resource regarding intake-related issues, i.e., determine jurisdiction, assist in clearing policy issues to process claim; in finding coverage or other information.

· May participate in training employees new to the role.

· Processes Workers’ Compensation claims retrieved from Open Pool queues or via telephone; codes body part, diagnosis and cause of injury by entering submitted data in the claims system reviews claim for accuracy prior to completion and performs all tasks specified for state-specific requirements after claim setup.

· Confirms policy coverage for date of injury, business location and injury location; requests policy update for locations as needed.

· Maintains department procedures, working instructions and job aides; may participate in creating new workflows or workflow changes.

· Researches multiple state and internal systems and documents and routes/or indexes incoming mail to appropriate region and/or department from unidentified mail queue.

· Forwards unidentified mail to sender using appropriate form letters.

· Routes documents to medical bill review vendor.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

Relevant combination of education and experience may be considered in lieu of degree.

A. EDUCATION REQUIRED:

High school diploma or G.E.D.

B. EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

Minimum of two years of general office experience, including customer service experience that provides the required skills, knowledge and abilities.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or

ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

OTHER SKILLS AND ABILITIES

· Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

· Ability to be an independent thinker to solve issues.

· Excellent organizational skills and ability to prioritize work to meet established deadlines.

· Basic knowledge of computers and spreadsheet software with data entry ability Basic knowledge of word processing software.

· Excellent customer service skills

· Knowledge of multi-functional telephone system.

· Ability to proofread correspondence for accuracy of spelling, grammar, punctuation and format.

· Ability to verify data for accuracy.

· Ability to multi-task i.e. interacts on telephone while entering data.

· Ability to work effectively with various business units.

· Ability to train and coach others to perform the core responsibilities.

· Ability to work varied hours/days/shifts.

C. ADDITIONAL EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND/OR ABILITIES PREFERRED:

· Insurance Institute of America (IIA) or other insurance related coursework.

· Knowledge of Workers Compensation or insurance.

· Basic knowledge of spreadsheet software.

· Knowledge of medical terminology.

· Knowledge of claims reporting process for multiple states.

· Experience using a document management system with workflows.

· Other insurance related coursework.

· Experience providing customer service over the phone.

· Excellent telephone etiquette.

Work is performed in an office setting with no unusual hazards. Work may be performed at varied hours/days/shifts.
